# Bestselling Canadian books of 2023

January 8, 2024

[Research & Analysis](https://booknetcanada.ca/category/research-analysis/)

At the end of last year, we showed you the [bestselling books of 2023](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2023/12/14/bestselling-books-of-2023). Before we get too far into this year, let’s look at the bestselling books by Canadian contributors last year.

The following lists are based on print sales volume in Canada from January 1, 2023, to December 3, 2023, according to [SalesData](https://booknetcanada.ca/salesdata), BookNet’s national sales tracking service for the Canadian English-language trade book market.

## [Top 10 bestselling Fiction books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727)

[![Image 2: Covers of Meet Me at the Lake by Carley Fortune, Everyone Here Is Lying by Shari Lapena, and The Defector by Chris Hadfield](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Fiction_1.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727)

1.   _Meet Me at the Lake_ by Carley Fortune🍁 (9780735243781)

2.   _Everyone Here Is Lying_ by Shari Lapena🍁 (9780385698900)

3.   _The Defector_ by Chris Hadfield🍁 (9781039005402)

4.   _Five Little Indians_ by Michelle Good🍁 (9781443459181)

5.   _A Death at the Party_ by Amy Stuart🍁 (9781668009109)

6.   _The Whispers_ by Ashley Audrain🍁 (9780735239937)

7.   _The Lie Maker_ by Linwood Barclay🍁 (9780063320598)

8.   _The Drowning Woman_ by Robyn Harding🍁 (9781538756966)

9.   _The Sleeping Car Porter_ by Suzette Mayr🍁 (9781552454589)

10.   _Everything She Feared_ by Rick Mofina🍁 (9780778334378)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727).

This list is quite different from [last year’s top 10](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022), with the exception of Michelle Good’s _Five Little Indians_, which was in the number one spot last year, and remains on this year’s list. Carley Fortune also returns to the list in 2023, but with a different book in 2023 than last year; in 2022, _Every Summer After_ was number two on the list.

Similar to last year, the majority of the books on this list, 80%, were frontlist — published in 2023. And there was one lone hardcover (Chris Hadfield’s _The Defector_) the rest were paperbacks.

## [Top 10 bestselling Non-Fiction books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730)

[![Image 3: Covers of Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts by Jillian Harris and Tori Wessze, Outlive by Peter Attia and Bill Gifford, and The Myth of Normal by Gabor Maté and Daniel Maté](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/NonFiction.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730)

1.   _Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts_ by Jillian Harris🍁 and Tori Wesszer🍁 (9780735240780)

2.   _Outlive_ by Peter Attia🍁 and Bill Gifford (9780593236598)

3.   _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté🍁 and Daniel Maté 🍁(9780735278363)

4.   _Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing_ by Matthew Perry🍁 (9781250866448)

5.   _12 Rules for Life_ by Jordan B. Peterson🍁 (9780345816023)

6.   _The Road Years_ by Rick Mercer🍁 (9780385688901)

7.   _Ducks_ by Kate Beaton🍁 (9781770462892)

8.   _When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté🍁 (9780676973129)

9.   _My Effin’ Life_ by Geddy Lee🍁 (9780063159419)

10.   _Love, Pamela_ by Pamela Anderson🍁 (9780063226562)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Non-Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730).

There’s more overlap between the[2022](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022) and 2023 Non-Fiction lists. Four books were repeats: _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté and Daniel Maté; _Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing_ by Matthew Perry; _12 Rules for Life_ by Jordan B. Peterson; and _When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté.

And on the flip side from the Fiction list above, there was only one paperback edition (_When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté) on the list, the remaining nine were all hardcovers.

## [Top 10 bestselling Juvenile and Young Adult books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732)

[![Image 4: Covers of Love You Forever by Robert Munsch, illus. by Sheila McGraw in three formats](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Juv26YA.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732)

1.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Paperback) (9780920668375)

2.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Board book) (9780228101048)

3.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Hardcover) (9780920668368)

4.   _Every Child Matters_ by Phyllis Webstad,🍁 illus by Karlene Harvey (9781778540165)

5.   _The Paper Bag Princess_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Michael Martchenko🍁 (9781773210292)

6.   _I Hope_ by Monique Gray Smith,🍁 illus. by Gabrielle Grimard🍁 (9781459825932)

7.   _Braiding Sweetgrass for Young Adults_ by Robin Wall Kimmerer and Monique Gray Smith,🍁 illus. by Nicole Neidhardt (9781728458991)

8.   _The Barren Grounds_ by David A. Robertson🍁 (9780735266124)

9.   _Dear Girl,_ by Amy Krouse Rosenthal and Paris Rosenthal, illus. by Holly Hatam 🍁 (9780062422507)

10.   _The Tryout: A Graphic Novel_ by Christina Soontornvat, illus. by Joanna Cacao 🍁 (9781338741261)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Juvenile & YA](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732).

It seems as though Canadian book buyers will love _Love You Forever_ forever – top spot since[2019](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2019/12/9/2019-bestsellers). Three different editions of the classic Robert Munsch title take the top three spots on the list this year. They were all on[last year’s list](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022), too, along with the other Robert Munch classic, _The Paper Bag Princess_. _The Barren Grounds_ by David A. Robertson was the last title to appear on both this year’s and last year’s lists.

The only title on the list published in 2023 was _Every Child Matters_ by Phyllis Webstad. The rest were backlist.

# Bestselling Canadian books of 2023

January 8, 2024

[Research & Analysis](https://booknetcanada.ca/category/research-analysis/)

At the end of last year, we showed you the [bestselling books of 2023](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2023/12/14/bestselling-books-of-2023). Before we get too far into this year, let’s look at the bestselling books by Canadian contributors last year.

The following lists are based on print sales volume in Canada from January 1, 2023, to December 3, 2023, according to [SalesData](https://booknetcanada.ca/salesdata), BookNet’s national sales tracking service for the Canadian English-language trade book market.

## [Top 10 bestselling Fiction books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727)

[![Image 2: Covers of Meet Me at the Lake by Carley Fortune, Everyone Here Is Lying by Shari Lapena, and The Defector by Chris Hadfield](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Fiction_1.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727)

1.   _Meet Me at the Lake_ by Carley Fortune🍁 (9780735243781)

2.   _Everyone Here Is Lying_ by Shari Lapena🍁 (9780385698900)

3.   _The Defector_ by Chris Hadfield🍁 (9781039005402)

4.   _Five Little Indians_ by Michelle Good🍁 (9781443459181)

5.   _A Death at the Party_ by Amy Stuart🍁 (9781668009109)

6.   _The Whispers_ by Ashley Audrain🍁 (9780735239937)

7.   _The Lie Maker_ by Linwood Barclay🍁 (9780063320598)

8.   _The Drowning Woman_ by Robyn Harding🍁 (9781538756966)

9.   _The Sleeping Car Porter_ by Suzette Mayr🍁 (9781552454589)

10.   _Everything She Feared_ by Rick Mofina🍁 (9780778334378)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727).

This list is quite different from [last year’s top 10](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022), with the exception of Michelle Good’s _Five Little Indians_, which was in the number one spot last year, and remains on this year’s list. Carley Fortune also returns to the list in 2023, but with a different book in 2023 than last year; in 2022, _Every Summer After_ was number two on the list.

Similar to last year, the majority of the books on this list, 80%, were frontlist — published in 2023. And there was one lone hardcover (Chris Hadfield’s _The Defector_) the rest were paperbacks.

## [Top 10 bestselling Non-Fiction books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730)

[![Image 3: Covers of Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts by Jillian Harris and Tori Wessze, Outlive by Peter Attia and Bill Gifford, and The Myth of Normal by Gabor Maté and Daniel Maté](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/NonFiction.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730)

1.   _Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts_ by Jillian Harris🍁 and Tori Wesszer🍁 (9780735240780)

2.   _Outlive_ by Peter Attia🍁 and Bill Gifford (9780593236598)

3.   _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté🍁 and Daniel Maté 🍁(9780735278363)

4.   _Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing_ by Matthew Perry🍁 (9781250866448)

5.   _12 Rules for Life_ by Jordan B. Peterson🍁 (9780345816023)

6.   _The Road Years_ by Rick Mercer🍁 (9780385688901)

7.   _Ducks_ by Kate Beaton🍁 (9781770462892)

8.   _When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté🍁 (9780676973129)

9.   _My Effin’ Life_ by Geddy Lee🍁 (9780063159419)

10.   _Love, Pamela_ by Pamela Anderson🍁 (9780063226562)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Non-Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730).

There’s more overlap between the[2022](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022) and 2023 Non-Fiction lists. Four books were repeats: _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté and Daniel Maté; _Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing_ by Matthew Perry; _12 Rules for Life_ by Jordan B. Peterson; and _When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté.

And on the flip side from the Fiction list above, there was only one paperback edition (_When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté) on the list, the remaining nine were all hardcovers.

## [Top 10 bestselling Juvenile and Young Adult books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732)

[![Image 4: Covers of Love You Forever by Robert Munsch, illus. by Sheila McGraw in three formats](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Juv26YA.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732)

1.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Paperback) (9780920668375)

2.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Board book) (9780228101048)

3.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Hardcover) (9780920668368)

4.   _Every Child Matters_ by Phyllis Webstad,🍁 illus by Karlene Harvey (9781778540165)

5.   _The Paper Bag Princess_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Michael Martchenko🍁 (9781773210292)

6.   _I Hope_ by Monique Gray Smith,🍁 illus. by Gabrielle Grimard🍁 (9781459825932)

7.   _Braiding Sweetgrass for Young Adults_ by Robin Wall Kimmerer and Monique Gray Smith,🍁 illus. by Nicole Neidhardt (9781728458991)

8.   _The Barren Grounds_ by David A. Robertson🍁 (9780735266124)

9.   _Dear Girl,_ by Amy Krouse Rosenthal and Paris Rosenthal, illus. by Holly Hatam 🍁 (9780062422507)

10.   _The Tryout: A Graphic Novel_ by Christina Soontornvat, illus. by Joanna Cacao 🍁 (9781338741261)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Juvenile & YA](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732).

It seems as though Canadian book buyers will love _Love You Forever_ forever – top spot since[2019](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2019/12/9/2019-bestsellers). Three different editions of the classic Robert Munsch title take the top three spots on the list this year. They were all on[last year’s list](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022), too, along with the other Robert Munch classic, _The Paper Bag Princess_. _The Barren Grounds_ by David A. Robertson was the last title to appear on both this year’s and last year’s lists.

The only title on the list published in 2023 was _Every Child Matters_ by Phyllis Webstad. The rest were backlist.

# Bestselling books of 2023

December 14, 2023

[Research & Analysis](https://booknetcanada.ca/category/research-analysis/)

It’s time for our annual bestselling books list. This year, we’ve identified the top-selling titles in the Fiction, Non-Fiction, and Juvenile & Young Adult categories.

The following lists are based on print sales volume in Canada from January 1, 2023, to December 3, 2023, according to [SalesData](https://booknetcanada.ca/salesdata), BookNet’s national sales tracking service for the Canadian English-language trade book market.

## [Top 10 bestselling Fiction books of 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238599)

[![Image 2: Collage of covers of It Starts with Us by Colleen Hoover, It Ends with Us by Colleen Hoover, and Fourth Wing by Rebecca Yarros.](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/FIC.jpg)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238599)

1.   _It Starts with Us_ by Colleen Hoover (9781668001226)

2.   _It Ends with Us_ by Colleen Hoover (9781501110368)

3.   _Fourth Wing_ by Rebecca Yarros (9781649374042)

4.   _Homecoming_ by Kate Morton (9781982149352)

5.   _The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo_ by Taylor Jenkins Reid (9781501161933)

6.   _Icebreaker_ by Hannah Grace (9781668026038)

7.   _Lessons in Chemistry_ by Bonnie Garmus (9780385697378)

8.   _Verity_ by Colleen Hoover (9781538724736)

9.   _Iron Flame_ by Rebecca Yarros (9781649374172)

10.   _Meet me at the Lake_ by Carley Fortune 🍁 (9780735243781)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238599).

There are four repeat titles from[last year’s](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022) bestselling Fiction list: Colleen Hoover’s _It Ends with Us_, _It Starts with Us_, and _Verity_ along with Taylor Jenkins Reid’s _The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo_ were featured. _It Ends with Us_ and _The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo_ have been featured on the bestselling Fiction list since [2021](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2021/12/20/bestselling-books-of-2021)!

Last year saw a majority of backlist titles — 70%, while [2021](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2021/12/20/bestselling-books-of-2021) and [2020](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2020/12/15/bestselling-books-of-2020) saw a majority of frontlist titles. However, this year, the list is 50% backlist and 50% frontlist and over half of the list is made up of romance titles.

## [Top 10 bestselling Non-Fiction books of 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238603)

[![Image 3: Collage of covers of Spare by Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex, Atomic Habits by James Clear, The Woman in Me by Britney Spears.](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/NONFIC.jpg)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238603)

1.   _Spare_ by Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex (9781039003750)

2.   _Atomic Habits_ by James Clear (9780735211292)

3.   _The Woman in Me_ by Britney Spears (9781668009048)

4.   _The 48 Laws of Power_ by Robert Greene and Joost Elffers (9780140280197)

5.   _Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts_ by Jillian Harris 🍁 and Tori Wesszer 🍁 (9780735240780)

6.   _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté 🍁 and Daniel Maté 🍁 (9780735278363)

7.   _Outlive_ by Peter Attia 🍁 and Bill Gifford (9780593236598)

8.   _The Psychology of Money_ by Morgan Housel (9780857197689)

9.   _The Body Keeps the Score_ by Bessel van der Kolk (9780143127741)

10.   _8 Rules of Love_ by Jay Shetty (9781982183066)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue:[Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Non-Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238603).

_The Body Keeps the Score_ by Bessel van der Kolk and _Atomic Habits_ by James Clear have been featured on the bestselling Non-Fiction list since [2021](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2021/12/20/bestselling-books-of-2021). _Atomic Habits_ has been number one the last two years but this year was dethroned by Spare and is now seated at number two. _The 48 Laws of Power_ by Robert Greene & Joost Elffers and _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté 🍁 & Daniel Maté 🍁 are repeat titles from [last year](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022).

Like the bestselling Fiction category, the the list is 50% backlist and 50% frontlist unlike [last year](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022) where the majority of the list was backlist titles.

# Bestselling books of 2023

December 14, 2023

[Research & Analysis](https://booknetcanada.ca/category/research-analysis/)

It’s time for our annual bestselling books list. This year, we’ve identified the top-selling titles in the Fiction, Non-Fiction, and Juvenile & Young Adult categories.

​In the dystopian world of [Cherie Dimaline](http://cbc.ca/1.4505184)'s award-winning [_The Marrow Thieves_](http://cbc.ca/1.4195121), climate change has ravaged the Earth and a continent-wide hunt and slaughter of Indigenous people is underway. Wanted for their bone marrow, which contains the lost ability to dream, a group of Indigenous people seek refuge in the old lands.

In 2017, [_The Marrow Thieves_](http://cbc.ca/1.4195121) won the [Governor General's Literary Award for Young people's literature — text](http://cbc.ca/1.4380043) and the [Kirkus Prize for young readers' literature](http://cbc.ca/1.4385744). It is [currently being adapted for television](http://cbc.ca/1.4643449). The sequel, [_Hunting by Stars_](http://cbc.ca/1.6090247)_,_ was released in 2021. [_The Marrow Thieves_](http://cbc.ca/1.4195121) was also defended by [Jully Black](http://cbc.ca/1.4503735) on [_Canada Reads_](http://cbc.ca/canadareads) 2018.

*   [**After blockbuster book**_**The Marrow Thieves**_**, 'peer pressure' led Cherie Dimaline to pen sequel**_**Hunting by Stars**_](https://www.cbc.ca/radio/thenextchapter/full-episode-oct-23-2021-1.6215510/after-blockbuster-book-the-marrow-thieves-peer-pressure-led-cherie-dimaline-to-pen-sequel-hunting-by-stars-1.6215513)

[Cherie Dimaline](http://cbc.ca/1.4505184) is a Métis author and editor. Her other books include [_Red Rooms_](http://cbc.ca/1.4511051), [_The Girl Who Grew a Galaxy_](http://cbc.ca/1.4012996)_,_[_A Gentle Habit_](http://cbc.ca/1.4129170) and [_Empire of Wild_](http://cbc.ca/1.5212680). [_The Marrow Thieves_](http://cbc.ca/1.4195121)was named one of [Time magazine's top 100 YA novels of all time](https://www.cbc.ca/books/4-canadian-titles-featured-in-time-s-100-best-ya-books-of-all-time-list-1.6140114). [Dimaline](http://cbc.ca/1.4505184) won [the 2021 Writers' Trust Engel Findley Award](https://www.cbc.ca/books/katherena-vermette-tomson-highway-and-cherie-dimaline-among-winners-at-2021-writers-trust-awards-1.6234384). The $25,000 recognizes the accomplishments of a fiction writer in the middle of their career.

With her dreams intensifying and getting more dangerous, Mackenzie must confront a violent family legacy and reconcile with the land and her community.

In [_The Myth of Normal_](http://cbc.ca/1.6565159), Gabor Maté examines why chronic illness and general health problems are on the rise in Western countries with good healthcare systems. Maté explains how Western medicine, while technologically advanced, fails to treat the whole person and ignores cultural stressors. Daniel Maté is a composer and lyricist whose musicals include _The Longing and the Short of It_, _Hansel & Gretl & Heidi & Gunter_ and _Middle School Mysteries_. He's received the Kleban Prize for Lyrics and the ASCAP Foundation Cole Porter Award.

## [**10.**_**Old Babes in the Wood**_**by Margaret Atwood**](https://www.cbc.ca/books/old-babes-in-the-woods-by-margaret-atwood-1.6736545)

![Image 5: A purple book cover featuring a close-up illustration of a white cat's face and a photo of the book's author, a woman with curly white hair sitting in front of a pink wall.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.6734864,1703703782000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C1938%2C1091%29%3B)

Old Babes in the Wood is a book by Margaret Atwood. (McClelland & Stewart, Luis Mora)

Margaret Atwood's latest is a collection of 15 stories that use narrative— and [Atwood](https://www.cbc.ca/1.4715044)'s signature intellect and wit — to speak to our modern times. At the centre of the collection are seven stories about a couple through the decades, mapping how their life evolves through the mundane and the extraordinary.

*   [81 surprising facts about Margaret Atwood](https://www.cbc.ca/books/81-surprising-facts-about-margaret-atwood-1.4091106)

Atwood is a celebrated Canadian writer who has published fiction, nonfiction, poetry and comics. Her acclaimed books include [_The Handmaid's Tale_](http://cbc.ca/1.3993722), [_Alias Grace_](http://cbc.ca/1.3969092), [_Oryx and Crake_](http://cbc.ca/1.3992161) and [_The Edible Woman_](http://cbc.ca/1.4005257). She has won several awards for her work including the Governor General's Literary Award, the Scotiabank [Giller Prize](https://www.cbc.ca/books/gillerprize) and the Booker Prize. She is also a founder of the Griffin Poetry Prize and the Writers' Trust of Canada.

## [**8.**_**The Marrow Thieves**_**by Cherie Dimaline**](http://cbc.ca/1.4195121)

![Image 8: A woman with glasses and long brown hair. A blue and purple book cover featuring half the face of a young boy with long brown hair.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.4952928,1678814851000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C702%2C405%29%3B)

Cherie Dimaline is the author of The Marrow Thieves. (Peter Power/CBC, Dancing Cat Books)

​In the dystopian world of [Cherie Dimaline](http://cbc.ca/1.4505184)'s award-winning [_The Marrow Thieves_](http://cbc.ca/1.4195121), climate change has ravaged the Earth and a continent-wide hunt and slaughter of Indigenous people is underway. Wanted for their bone marrow, which contains the lost ability to dream, a group of Indigenous people seek refuge in the old lands.

In 2017, [_The Marrow Thieves_](http://cbc.ca/1.4195121) won the [Governor General's Literary Award for Young people's literature — text](http://cbc.ca/1.4380043) and the [Kirkus Prize for young readers' literature](http://cbc.ca/1.4385744). It is [currently being adapted for television](http://cbc.ca/1.4643449). The sequel, [_Hunting by Stars_](http://cbc.ca/1.6090247)_,_ was released in 2021. [_The Marrow Thieves_](http://cbc.ca/1.4195121) was also defended by [Jully Black](http://cbc.ca/1.4503735) on [_Canada Reads_](http://cbc.ca/canadareads) 2018.

*   [**After blockbuster book**_**The Marrow Thieves**_**, 'peer pressure' led Cherie Dimaline to pen sequel**_**Hunting by Stars**_](https://www.cbc.ca/radio/thenextchapter/full-episode-oct-23-2021-1.6215510/after-blockbuster-book-the-marrow-thieves-peer-pressure-led-cherie-dimaline-to-pen-sequel-hunting-by-stars-1.6215513)

[Cherie Dimaline](http://cbc.ca/1.4505184) is a Métis author and editor. Her other books include [_Red Rooms_](http://cbc.ca/1.4511051), [_The Girl Who Grew a Galaxy_](http://cbc.ca/1.4012996)_,_[_A Gentle Habit_](http://cbc.ca/1.4129170) and [_Empire of Wild_](http://cbc.ca/1.5212680). [_The Marrow Thieves_](http://cbc.ca/1.4195121)was named one of [Time magazine's top 100 YA novels of all time](https://www.cbc.ca/books/4-canadian-titles-featured-in-time-s-100-best-ya-books-of-all-time-list-1.6140114). [Dimaline](http://cbc.ca/1.4505184) won [the 2021 Writers' Trust Engel Findley Award](https://www.cbc.ca/books/katherena-vermette-tomson-highway-and-cherie-dimaline-among-winners-at-2021-writers-trust-awards-1.6234384). The $25,000 recognizes the accomplishments of a fiction writer in the middle of their career.

## [**7.**_**The Sleeping Car Porter**_**by Suzette Mayr**](https://www.cbc.ca/1.6564652)

![Image 10: A book cover featuring a dapper man in a boat hat and the book's author, a woman with gray and black hair holding a glass trophy and wearing a blue blazer.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.6644014,1686754301000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C850%2C478%29%3B)

The Sleeping Car Porter is a novel by Suzette Mayr. (Coach House, Ryan Emberley)

[_The Sleeping Car Porter_](http://cbc.ca/1.6564652) tells the story of Baxter, a Black man in 1929 who works as a sleeping car porter on a train that travels across the country. He smiles and tries to be invisible to the passengers, but what he really wants is to save up and go to dentistry school. On one particular trip out west, the train is stalled and Baxter finds a naughty postcard of two gay men. The postcard reawakens his memories and longings and puts his job in jeopardy.

[_The Sleeping Car Porter_](http://cbc.ca/1.6564652) won [the 2022 Scotiabank Giller Prize](https://www.cbc.ca/1.6643257).

*   [**Suzette Mayr's novel**_**The Sleeping Car Porter**_**uses magic realism to highlight Black Canadian history**](http://cbc.ca/1.6630157)

Suzette Mayr is a poet and novelist based in Calgary. She is the author of the novels [_Dr. Edith Vane and the Hares of Crawley Hall_](http://cbc.ca/1.3974510), [_Monoceros_](http://cbc.ca/1.4022309), _Moon Honey_,_The Widows_ and _Venous Hum_.

## [**6.**_**Bad Cree**_**by Jessica Johns**](https://www.cbc.ca/books/bad-cree-by-jessica-johns-1.6707974)

![Image 11: Composite image of a red book cover and a woman with dark hair and glasses standing in front of a blue wall and looking to the side](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.6975583,1695404153000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C620%2C349%29%3B)

Bad Cree is a novel by Jessica Johns. (HarperCollins Canada, Loretta Johns)

[_Bad Cree_](http://cbc.ca/1.6707974) is a horror-infused novel that centres around a young woman named Mackenzie, who is haunted by terrifying nightmares and wracked with guilt about her sister Sabrina's untimely death. The lines between her dreams and reality start to blur when she begins seeing a murder of crows following her around the city — and starts getting threatening text messages from someone claiming to be her dead sister. Looking to escape, Mackenzie heads back to her hometown in rural Alberta where she finds her family still entrenched in their grief. With her dreams intensifying and getting more dangerous, Mackenzie must confront a violent family legacy and reconcile with the land and her community.

*   [**Jessica Johns's novel**_**Bad Cree**_**is a story about grief, guilt and healing**](https://www.cbc.ca/books/jessica-johns-s-novel-bad-cree-is-a-story-about-grief-guilt-and-healing-read-an-excerpt-now-1.6707897)

Jessica Johns is a Vancouver-based writer, visual artist and member of Sucker Creek First Nation in Treaty 8 Territory in northern Alberta. Johns won the [2020 Writers' Trust Journey Prize](http://cbc.ca/1.5770790) for the short story _Bad Cree_, which evolved into the novel of the same name.

![Image 13: Women Talking by Miriam Toews. Illustrated book cover and portrait of white female young author.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.4768346,1703701293000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C620%2C349%29%3B)

Women Talking is Miriam Toews's latest novel. (Carol Loewen, Knopf Canada)

​In [Miriam Toews](http://cbc.ca/1.4716329)'s powerful novel, eight Mennonite women come together to talk. Why? They have 48 hours to make a decision that will impact every woman and child in their community. [_Women Talking_](http://cbc.ca/1.4726235) is inspired by the real-life case in the 2000s, when women in a Bolivian Mennonite community began whispering that they were waking up groggy, in pain, feeling like they had been sexually molested.

[_Women Talking_](http://cbc.ca/1.4726235) was a [finalist for the 2018 Governor General's Literary Award for fiction](http://cbc.ca/1.4840600).

*   [**The real-life 'ghost rapes' that inspired Miriam Toews's new novel,**_**Women Talking**_](http://cbc.ca/1.4861095)

Toews is the author of several acclaimed novels, including [_A Complicated Kindness_](https://www.cbc.ca/1.3991966), which won the Governor General's Literary Award for English-language fiction in 2004 and won [_Canada Reads_](http://cbc.ca/canadareads) in 2006, and [_All My Puny Sorrows_](http://www.cbc.ca/1.3972824)_,_ which won the 2014 Rogers Writers' Trust Fiction Prize and was shortlisted for the 2014 Scotiabank Giller Prize.

## [**4.**_**The Myth of Normal**_**by Gabor Maté with Daniel Maté**](https://www.cbc.ca/books/the-myth-of-normal-1.6565159)

![Image 14: Two men with short dark hair, their portraits are on either side of a yellow and red book cover with an abstract silhouette of a head.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.6571775,1678814755000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C1600%2C900%29%3B)

The Myth of Normal is a book by Gabor Maté and Daniel Maté. (Knopf Canada, Ken Wilkinson)

In [_The Myth of Normal_](http://cbc.ca/1.6565159), Gabor Maté examines why chronic illness and general health problems are on the rise in Western countries with good healthcare systems. Maté explains how Western medicine, while technologically advanced, fails to treat the whole person and ignores cultural stressors. With his son Daniel, Maté untangles common myths about what makes us sick and offers a guide on health and healing.

*   [**Treating addiction requires both science and compassion, says Dr. Gabor Maté**](http://cbc.ca/1.4792095)

Gabor Maté is a doctor and an expert on topics such as addiction, stress and childhood development. He's the author of several books, including [_In the Realm of Hungry Ghosts_](http://cbc.ca/1.4200078), _When the Body Says_ and _The Cost of Hidden Stress_.

Daniel Maté is a composer and lyricist whose musicals include _The Longing and the Short of It_, _Hansel & Gretl & Heidi & Gunter_ and _Middle School Mysteries_. He's received the Kleban Prize for Lyrics and the ASCAP Foundation Cole Porter Award.

## [**3.**_**Five Little Indians**_**by Michelle Good**](http://cbc.ca/1.5451966)

Five Little Indians is a novel by Michelle Good. (HarperCollins, Silken Sellinger Photography)

In [_Five Little Indians_](http://cbc.ca/1.5451966), Kenny, Lucy, Clara, Howie and Maisie were taken from their families and sent to a residential school when they were very small. Barely out of childhood, they are released and left to contend with the seedy world of eastside Vancouver. Fuelled by the trauma of their childhood, the five friends cross paths over the decades and struggle with the weight of their shared past.

[_Five Little Indians_](http://cbc.ca/1.5451966) won the [Amazon First Novel Award in 2021](https://www.cbc.ca/books/five-little-indians-by-michelle-good-wins-60k-amazon-first-novel-award-1.6044056) and won [_Canada Reads_ in 2022, championed by Ojibway author and Vogue fashion writer Christian Allaire.](https://www.cbc.ca/books/canadareads/christian-allaire-championing-five-little-indians-by-michelle-good-wins-canada-reads-2022-1.6403622)

*   [**Michelle Good's**_**Five Little Indians**_**is a fictional look at the real Canadian legacy of residential schools**](https://www.cbc.ca/radio/thenextchapter/full-episode-aug-31-2020-1.5559811/michelle-good-s-five-little-indians-is-a-fictional-look-at-the-real-canadian-legacy-of-residential-schools-1.5559853)

Good is a Cree writer and lawyer who is a member of Red Pheasant Cree Nation in Saskatchewan. She was named by [CBC Books in 2020 as a writer to watch.](http://cbc.ca/1.5666130) She is also the author of the essay collection [_Truth Telling_](https://www.cbc.ca/books/truth-telling-by-michelle-good-1.6819552).

Michael Christie is the author of Greenwood. (McClelland & Stewart, Cedar Bowers)

In the novel [_Greenwood_](http://cbc.ca/1.5212395), it's the year 2038 and most of the world has suffered from an environmental collapse. [_Greenwood_](http://cbc.ca/1.5212395) was a finalist [on Canada Reads in 2023, championed by actor Keegan Connor Tracy.](https://cbc.ca/books/canadareads/keegan-connor-tracy-champions-greenwood-by-michael-christie-on-canada-reads-2023-1.6716840)

[Michael Christie](http://www.cbc.ca/1.4793817) is a novelist who grew up in northern Ontario and currently lives in Victoria. His 2011 short story collection [_The Beggar's Garden_](http://cbc.ca/1.4805296) won the Vancouver Book Award and was a finalist for the Rogers Writers' Trust Fiction Prize. His 2015 novel [_If I Fall, If I Die_](http://cbc.ca/1.4017049)won the Northern Lit Award and was longlisted for the [Scotiabank Giller Prize](https://www.cbc.ca/books/gillerprize).

![Image 17: A composite image of a woman with dark brown hair smiling into the camera and a book cartoon book cover with a woman standing on the steps of a bulldozer looking off into the distance.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.6916904,1690292460000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C1920%2C1080%29%3B)

Kate Beaton is the author of Canada Reads-winning graphic memoir Ducks. (Corey Katz, Drawn & Quarterly)

[_Ducks_](http://cbc.ca/1.6559688) is an autobiographical graphic novel that recounts Beaton's time working in the Alberta oil sands between 2005 and 2008. With the goal of paying off her student loans, Beaton leaves her tight-knit seaside Nova Scotia community and heads west, where she encounters harsh realities, including the everyday trauma that no one discusses.

[_Ducks_](http://cbc.ca/1.6559688) won [_Canada Reads_](http://cbc.ca/canadareads) 2023, when it was [defended by _Jeopardy!_ super-champ Mattea Roach](https://www.cbc.ca/books/canadareads/mattea-roach-championing-ducks-by-kate-beaton-wins-canada-reads-2023-1.6795030).

*   [Kate Beaton's affecting Ducks dives into the lonely life of labour in Alberta's oil sands](https://www.cbc.ca/radio/thenextchapter/kate-beaton-s-affecting-ducks-dives-into-the-lonely-life-of-labour-in-alberta-s-oil-sands-1.6669384)

Beaton launched her career by publishing the comic strip [_Hark! A Vagrant_](http://cbc.ca/1.4720792)online. The sassy historical webcomic gained a following of 500,000 monthly visitors and was eventually turned into a bestselling book.

Her success continued with the book [_Step Aside, Pops!_](http://cbc.ca/1.4011766)and two children's books, [_King Baby_](http://cbc.ca/1.4024456) and [_The Princess and the Pony_](http://cbc.ca/1.4024415).

In this article, we look at the 33 best selling books of 2023. You can skip our detailed analysis of the publishing industry and head over directly to the [**10 Best Selling Books of 2023**](https://www.insidermonkey.com/blog/10-best-selling-books-of-2023-1164109/).

WordsRated is a research organization that tracks trends in the books and publishing industry. According to its report titled [_Global Book Sales Statistics_](https://wordsrated.com/global-book-sales-statistics/#:~:text=As%20of%202023%2C%20the%20global,to%202021%2C%20with%20%2476.14%20billion.), the global book sales revenue was estimated to be slightly over $78 billion in 2023 - which is 2.53% higher than last year. This is an encouraging figure, considering that sales had dropped by over 10% in 2022 compared to 2021.

Over 2.2 billion books are sold each year. The US, China, UK, Germany, and Japan are the **top five book buying countries,** accounting for nearly two-thirds of the global book sales. Their share is likely to rise further to 68% by 2027.

However, trends in the book market are changing. Brick and mortar bookshops account for only 50.3% of the global revenue from book sales. Today, more than 25% of the books are sold through online channels. E-books, or electronic books, are also a phenomenon that is growing in popularity. Texts and images are displayed digitally, allowing readers to read books on their smartphones, tabs, or computer screens. The concept first emerged in the 1990s, with companies selling book content for reading on personal digital assistants (PDA). It has seen a boom since Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:[AMZN](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/amazon+com+inc/1018724/)) launched Kindle, its e-reading device, in 2007. According to the PEW Research Center, [30%](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2022/01/06/three-in-ten-americans-now-read-e-books/) of Americans now read e-books.

Another change has been the advent of audiobooks, which is the **fastest growing segment in the books industry**. Audio books are audio recordings of books being read out loud. Global audiobook revenue is estimated to reach $5.16 billion in 2023. In 2021, more than [$1.8](https://wordsrated.com/audiobook-sales-statistics/) billion worth of sales were generated from this segment in the United States. Audio books are quickly becoming the preferred mode of books for people belonging to low income groups. Percentage of adults with an annual household income of under $30,000, who have listened to an audiobook, increased from 14% in 2019 to 22% in 2022, as per a survey by PEW.

Due to a drop in print book sales revenue globally and other business reasons, Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) in March, this year, announced the closure of all of its physical bookstores in the US. However, print book sales still make up nearly 80% of the industry revenue. Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. (NYSE:[BNED](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/barnes+%26+noble+education+inc/1634117/)) is the **largest bookstore chain in the US** having presence in 627 locations. In 2022, Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. (NYSE:BNED) had a revenue of $1.5 billion.

Story Continues

In the books publishing industry, some of the biggest companies currently are Pearson plc (NYSE:[PSO](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/pearson+plc/938323/)), Penguin Random House, HarperCollins, and Simon & Schuster. Pearson plc (NYSE:PSO) publishes textbooks and digital courses for teachers, and has operations in more than 70 countries. The revenue of Pearson plc (NYSE:PSO) was $4.88 billion in 2022.

Penguin Random House publishes more than 1,500 books every year in various genres. HarperCollins' print and digital catalog is close to 0.2 million titles, with the company recording a revenue of $2.19 billion in FY 2022. Simon & Schuster is another major billion dollar publishing company; a lot of its books are sold on Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN). You can read more on this in our article, [**20 Biggest Publishing Companies in the World**](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/20-biggest-publishing-companies-world-133603045.html).

Before we head over to the list of the **best selling books of 2023**, it requires mention of some of the best selling books, series and authors of all time. Don Quixote, with 500 million copies sold is the **best selling book of all time**. The Spanish novel authored by Miguel de Cervantes was released in two volumes in 1605 and 1615. Whereas Harry Potter is the **best selling series****of all time** with 450 million copies sold. Unsurprisingly, William Shakespeare tops the list of the **best selling fiction authors** in history, with an estimated three billion copies of his books being [sold](https://wordsrated.com/best-selling-authors-statistics/).

### Methodology

The top 100 books on Amazon, and all 11 categories of bestsellers on The New York Times Company (NYSE:[NYT](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/new+york+times+co/71691/)) were carefully analyzed to build a pool of the bestselling books in the industry. Once that was determined, we ranked the best 33 books based on their number of copies sold in 2022 or 2023, or both. Information was obtained from various sources such as Amazon, The New York Times, Literary Hub, Publishers Weekly, Barnes & Noble, and Forbes, among others. In the case of estimated number of books sold being the same for two or more books, we used their publishing year as tie-breaker - the book which was published earlier and still remains a bestseller outranked the one that was released later.

33 Best Selling Books of 2023 

Let's head over to the **33 best selling books of 2023**.

### 33. Things We Never Got Over

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 50,906_**

Written by Lucy Score, Things We Never Got Over is an exceptional story of a woman who rediscovers herself after a relationship breakup and falls in love with a wealthy bar owner. An estimated 50,906 copies have been sold since its release in 2022 according to Publishers Weekly.

### 32. I Will Teach You To Be Rich

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 71,400_**

Authored by Ramit Sethi, this is a 2009 personal finance book that is currently on seventh place in The New York Times Company (NYSE:NYT) bestseller list in the self-help category. Over [1 million](https://cultivatingcash.com/teach-you-to-be-rich/) copies of the book have been sold so far, an estimated 71,400 of which were in 2022.

### 31. Outlive: The Science and Art of Longevity

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 82,907_**

Outlive was ranked among the top books on **New York Times' bestsellers list**in the nonfiction category. It is a great book for those who are interested in adopting a healthy lifestyle and prolonging their lives.

### 30. The Housemaid

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.1 million_**

Fiction novel written by Freida McFadden is a riveting story that is currently among the **top selling books of 2023**.

### 29. Happy Place

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.2 million_**

Happy Place was released in April 25, 2023, and is authored by Emily Henry who is widely known for writing romance novels. Happy Place is also based on friendship and love. Close to 0.2 million copies have been sold so far between the studied period of 2022-23.

### 28. Dog Man: Twenty Thousand Fleas Under the Sea

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.38 million_**

This is the 11th book in Dav Pilkey's Dog Man series and was released this year. It is among the top 20 on Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:[AMZN](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/amazon+com+inc/1018724/))'s 2023 best sellers list, and is highly popular among children.

### 27. Maybe Someday

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.54 million_**

Colleen Hoover's Maybe Someday is next on our list. It sold 543,658 copies in 2022 according to Literary Hub.

### 26. Brown Bear, Brown Bear, What Do You See?

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.58 million_**

Released in 1967, children's picture book authored by Bill Martin Jr. still remains a bestseller in 2023. Last year it sold an estimated 0.58 million books to earn a place in the **33 best selling books of 2023**.

### 25. The Four Agreements: A Practical Guide to Personal Freedom

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.6 million_**

The self-help book published in 1997 and authored by Don Miguel Ruiz has still managed to be among the **best selling books in 2023** more than two decades later. Text in the book is focused on the code of conduct based on ancient Toltec wisdom. A little over 0.6 million copies were sold in 2022.

### 24. Fairy Tale

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.627 million_**

Fairy Tale has sold 627,598 copies since its release in 2022. It is authored by Stephen King, and remains a best seller in 2023 as well.

### 23. Oh, the Places You'll Go!

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.628 million_**

More than three decades after its release in 1990, the book is still among the **best selling books of 2023** on Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN). The children's book is authored by Dr. Seuss. It sold 0.628 million copies according to Publishers Weekly last year.

### 22. The Body Keeps the Score: Brain, Mind, and Body in the Healing of Trauma

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.638 million_**

Authored by prominent psychiatrist Bessel van der Kolk, this book explores how trauma affects the human body, including the brain. More than two million copies of the book have been sold since it was published in 2014. Number of copies sold in 2022 were 638,831.

### 21. It Ends with Us

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.67 million_**

It Ends with Us, authored by Colleen Hoover, who has also written many other books covered in this article, is next on our list. The book is based on the relationship between her parents. More than 4 million copies of the book have been sold since its release in 2016. In 2022, an estimated 0.67 million copies were sold.

### 20. The Very Hungry Caterpillar

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.74 million_**

Eric Carle's 1969 children's picture book, The Very Hungry Caterpillar, is the story of a caterpillar that is hungry and eats a variety of foods before becoming a butterfly. The book is available in more than 60 languages. Over [50](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-57263822) million copies have been sold since its publication. 738,840 of these were sold last year according to Publishers Weekly.

### 19. Verity

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.75 million_**

Verity is one of the **most sold books of 2023**. Authored by Colleen Hoover, it finds a place on the bestsellers lists of both Amazon and New York Times with 0.75 million copies sold in 2022.

### 18. Diper Överlöde

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.83 million_**

Jeff Kinney's Diper Överlöde is the 11th book in the Diary of a Wimpy Kid series. It has sold an estimated 0.83 million copies since its release in October 2022.

### 17. November 9

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.99 million_**

The New York Times' bestseller November 9 sold close to one million copies in 2022. The book is based on a love story between an aspiring novelist and his unexpected muse.

### 16. Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 1 million_**

Amazon named Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow as the **best book of 2022**. Released in July last year, it is among the **top most selling books of 2023** as well. Paramount Pictures, in 2021, locked a $2 million [deal](https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/paramount-pictures-locks-2-million-170407735.html) for film rights of this book.

### 15. Icebreaker

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 1 million_**

Next on our list is Hannah Grace's book, Icebreaker, which was named among the Top 100 Best Sellers on Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) in 2023. Icebreaker is fourth on the paperback fiction **best sellers list** of The New York Times Company (NYSE:NYT). It was released in November 2022, and has since sold an estimated one million copies according to Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. (NYSE:BNED).

### 14. The Last Thing He Told Me

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 1 million_**

The Last Thing He Told Me has spent 65 weeks on New York Times' best sellers list. The mystery thriller novel was published in May 2021 by Simon & Schuster, and is authored by Laura Dave.

### 13. Reminders of Him

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 1.3 million_**

Released in January 2022, this is a story of a mother released from prison after five years, returns to her town with the hope to reunite with her daughter. Around 1.3 million copies of the book has been sold since it was published. It is authored by Colleen Hoover.

### 12. The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 1.3 million_**

The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo is a fictional novel authored by Taylor Jenkins Reid, and published in 2017 by Atria Books. The plot is based on the life of Evelyn Hugo, a fictional Hollywood star. The book is ranked 11th on Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)'s list of bestsellers in 2023 despite being released six years ago in 2017.

### 11. Ugly Love

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 1.45 million_**

Colleen Hoover's Ugly Love is a heart wrenching love story, with the plot centered around love at first sight which went wrong. The writer has also authored best sellers _It Starts with Us_, and _It Ends with Us_.

In this article, we look at the 33 best selling books of 2023. You can skip our detailed analysis of the publishing industry and head over directly to the [**10 Best Selling Books of 2023**](https://www.insidermonkey.com/blog/10-best-selling-books-of-2023-1164109/).

WordsRated is a research organization that tracks trends in the books and publishing industry. According to its report titled [_Global Book Sales Statistics_](https://wordsrated.com/global-book-sales-statistics/#:~:text=As%20of%202023%2C%20the%20global,to%202021%2C%20with%20%2476.14%20billion.), the global book sales revenue was estimated to be slightly over $78 billion in 2023 - which is 2.53% higher than last year. This is an encouraging figure, considering that sales had dropped by over 10% in 2022 compared to 2021.

Over 2.2 billion books are sold each year. The US, China, UK, Germany, and Japan are the **top five book buying countries,** accounting for nearly two-thirds of the global book sales. Their share is likely to rise further to 68% by 2027.

However, trends in the book market are changing. Brick and mortar bookshops account for only 50.3% of the global revenue from book sales. Today, more than 25% of the books are sold through online channels. E-books, or electronic books, are also a phenomenon that is growing in popularity. Texts and images are displayed digitally, allowing readers to read books on their smartphones, tabs, or computer screens. The concept first emerged in the 1990s, with companies selling book content for reading on personal digital assistants (PDA). It has seen a boom since Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:[AMZN](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/amazon+com+inc/1018724/)) launched Kindle, its e-reading device, in 2007. According to the PEW Research Center, [30%](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2022/01/06/three-in-ten-americans-now-read-e-books/) of Americans now read e-books.

Another change has been the advent of audiobooks, which is the **fastest growing segment in the books industry**. Audio books are audio recordings of books being read out loud. Global audiobook revenue is estimated to reach $5.16 billion in 2023. In 2021, more than [$1.8](https://wordsrated.com/audiobook-sales-statistics/) billion worth of sales were generated from this segment in the United States. Audio books are quickly becoming the preferred mode of books for people belonging to low income groups. Percentage of adults with an annual household income of under $30,000, who have listened to an audiobook, increased from 14% in 2019 to 22% in 2022, as per a survey by PEW.

Due to a drop in print book sales revenue globally and other business reasons, Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) in March, this year, announced the closure of all of its physical bookstores in the US. However, print book sales still make up nearly 80% of the industry revenue. Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. (NYSE:[BNED](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/barnes+%26+noble+education+inc/1634117/)) is the **largest bookstore chain in the US** having presence in 627 locations. In 2022, Barnes & Noble Education, Inc. (NYSE:BNED) had a revenue of $1.5 billion.

Story Continues

In the books publishing industry, some of the biggest companies currently are Pearson plc (NYSE:[PSO](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/pearson+plc/938323/)), Penguin Random House, HarperCollins, and Simon & Schuster. Pearson plc (NYSE:PSO) publishes textbooks and digital courses for teachers, and has operations in more than 70 countries. The revenue of Pearson plc (NYSE:PSO) was $4.88 billion in 2022.

Penguin Random House publishes more than 1,500 books every year in various genres. HarperCollins' print and digital catalog is close to 0.2 million titles, with the company recording a revenue of $2.19 billion in FY 2022. Simon & Schuster is another major billion dollar publishing company; a lot of its books are sold on Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN). You can read more on this in our article, [**20 Biggest Publishing Companies in the World**](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/20-biggest-publishing-companies-world-133603045.html).

Before we head over to the list of the **best selling books of 2023**, it requires mention of some of the best selling books, series and authors of all time. Don Quixote, with 500 million copies sold is the **best selling book of all time**. The Spanish novel authored by Miguel de Cervantes was released in two volumes in 1605 and 1615. Whereas Harry Potter is the **best selling series****of all time** with 450 million copies sold. Unsurprisingly, William Shakespeare tops the list of the **best selling fiction authors** in history, with an estimated three billion copies of his books being [sold](https://wordsrated.com/best-selling-authors-statistics/).

### Methodology

The top 100 books on Amazon, and all 11 categories of bestsellers on The New York Times Company (NYSE:[NYT](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/new+york+times+co/71691/)) were carefully analyzed to build a pool of the bestselling books in the industry. Once that was determined, we ranked the best 33 books based on their number of copies sold in 2022 or 2023, or both. Information was obtained from various sources such as Amazon, The New York Times, Literary Hub, Publishers Weekly, Barnes & Noble, and Forbes, among others. In the case of estimated number of books sold being the same for two or more books, we used their publishing year as tie-breaker - the book which was published earlier and still remains a bestseller outranked the one that was released later.

Let's head over to the **33 best selling books of 2023**.

### 33. Things We Never Got Over

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 50,906_**

Written by Lucy Score, Things We Never Got Over is an exceptional story of a woman who rediscovers herself after a relationship breakup and falls in love with a wealthy bar owner. An estimated 50,906 copies have been sold since its release in 2022 according to Publishers Weekly.

### 32. I Will Teach You To Be Rich

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 71,400_**

Authored by Ramit Sethi, this is a 2009 personal finance book that is currently on seventh place in The New York Times Company (NYSE:NYT) bestseller list in the self-help category. Over [1 million](https://cultivatingcash.com/teach-you-to-be-rich/) copies of the book have been sold so far, an estimated 71,400 of which were in 2022.

### 31. Outlive: The Science and Art of Longevity

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 82,907_**

Outlive was ranked among the top books on **New York Times' bestsellers list**in the nonfiction category. It is a great book for those who are interested in adopting a healthy lifestyle and prolonging their lives.

### 30. The Housemaid

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.1 million_**

Fiction novel written by Freida McFadden is a riveting story that is currently among the **top selling books of 2023**.

### 29. Happy Place

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.2 million_**

Happy Place was released in April 25, 2023, and is authored by Emily Henry who is widely known for writing romance novels. Happy Place is also based on friendship and love. Close to 0.2 million copies have been sold so far between the studied period of 2022-23.

### 28. Dog Man: Twenty Thousand Fleas Under the Sea

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.38 million_**

This is the 11th book in Dav Pilkey's Dog Man series and was released this year. It is among the top 20 on Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:[AMZN](https://www.insidermonkey.com/insider-trading/company/amazon+com+inc/1018724/))'s 2023 best sellers list, and is highly popular among children.

### 27. Maybe Someday

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.54 million_**

Colleen Hoover's Maybe Someday is next on our list. It sold 543,658 copies in 2022 according to Literary Hub.

### 26. Brown Bear, Brown Bear, What Do You See?

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.58 million_**

Released in 1967, children's picture book authored by Bill Martin Jr. still remains a bestseller in 2023. Last year it sold an estimated 0.58 million books to earn a place in the **33 best selling books of 2023**.

### 25. The Four Agreements: A Practical Guide to Personal Freedom

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.6 million_**

The self-help book published in 1997 and authored by Don Miguel Ruiz has still managed to be among the **best selling books in 2023** more than two decades later. Text in the book is focused on the code of conduct based on ancient Toltec wisdom. A little over 0.6 million copies were sold in 2022.

### 24. Fairy Tale

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.627 million_**

Fairy Tale has sold 627,598 copies since its release in 2022. It is authored by Stephen King, and remains a best seller in 2023 as well.

### 23. Oh, the Places You'll Go!

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.628 million_**

More than three decades after its release in 1990, the book is still among the **best selling books of 2023** on Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN). The children's book is authored by Dr. Seuss. It sold 0.628 million copies according to Publishers Weekly last year.

### 22. The Body Keeps the Score: Brain, Mind, and Body in the Healing of Trauma

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.638 million_**

### 21. It Ends with Us

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.67 million_**

It Ends with Us, authored by Colleen Hoover, who has also written many other books covered in this article, is next on our list. The book is based on the relationship between her parents. More than 4 million copies of the book have been sold since its release in 2016. In 2022, an estimated 0.67 million copies were sold.

### 20. The Very Hungry Caterpillar

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.74 million_**

Eric Carle's 1969 children's picture book, The Very Hungry Caterpillar, is the story of a caterpillar that is hungry and eats a variety of foods before becoming a butterfly. The book is available in more than 60 languages. Over [50](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-57263822) million copies have been sold since its publication. 738,840 of these were sold last year according to Publishers Weekly.

### 19. Verity

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.75 million_**

Verity is one of the **most sold books of 2023**. Authored by Colleen Hoover, it finds a place on the bestsellers lists of both Amazon and New York Times with 0.75 million copies sold in 2022.

### 18. Diper Överlöde

**_Estimated Copies Sold: 0.83 million_**

Jeff Kinney's Diper Överlöde is the 11th book in the Diary of a Wimpy Kid series. It has sold an estimated 0.83 million copies since its release in October 2022.

By Sarah Murdoch Special to the Star

The top 10 titles on the Original Fiction list are all by and for women— and young women at that: Witness the number of romances and tales of dragon-slaying teenaged girls. Last year there was plenty of romance but not a single fantasy title. We can thank TikTok for drawing together this huge community of adventure-craving readers. On the second half of our Top 20, men wrote just three of the novels: Stephen King (“Holly”), John Grisham (“The Exchange”) and Abraham Verghese (“The Covenant of Water”).

Here’s an interesting anomaly: While only three of 20 authors on the Original Fiction list are men, on the Canadian Fiction list, six of the 20 are men.

The titles on the 2023 Original Non-Fiction list is dominated by biographies and memoirs from both sexes.

Other reflections on the year in books:

*   Last year, romance writer Colleen Hoover held the top two spots with “It Ends with Us” and its sequel, “It Starts with Us.” Same this year. How boring. But her reign on the Fiction list is likely over. Hoover had seven books on the Top 20 list in 2022 but just three (just!) this year (the third, “Ugly Love,” chimes in at No. 15). CoHo was last seen on our regular weekly list on Sept. 6, when “It Ends with Us” ranked No. 10. She also ranks No. 1 on our bestselling Mystery list with “Verity,” beating out novels by veterans Stephen King and John Grisham.
*   Untimely death seems to spur book sales. Note that Matthew Perry’s 2022 memoir “Friends, Lovers and the Big Terrible Thing,” ended the year at No. 4 on the Original non-fiction list, because his death at the end of October sparked renewed interest in his life and travails. The book ended 2022 on the same list at #3.
*   Diversity, equity and inclusion have been hot topics and publishing houses and awards committees have been prompted to search for and encourage books by racialized writers. But has the push for equity paid off financially? The bestselling fiction of the year is almost entirely monochromatic: white women. The two exceptions are Chinese-American writer R.F. Kuang (“Yellowface”) and South-Asian author Abraham Verghese (“The Covenant of Water”). The only diversity on the Original non-fiction list is “Beyond the Story,” a 10 th anniversary coffee-table tome celebrating Korean boy group BTS, and “21 Things You May Not Know about the Indian Act” by Bob Joseph, a member of the Gwawaenuk Nation in British Columbia. The Canadian lists feature a greater representation: Cree writer Michelle Good; Anishinaabe writer Waubgeshig Rice, Suzette Mayr, a writer and academic of German and Afro-Caribbean background, Ted Nolan, a member of the Garden River First Nation Reserve, and writer and former politician Jody Wilson-Raybould, a member of the We Wai Kai Nation of British Columbia.
*   And finally, the top three books of the year, across all categories:

1.“Spare,” by Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex

2.“Twenty Thousand Fleas under the Sea (Dog Man #11)”, by Dav Pilkey

3.“It Starts with Us,” by Colleen Hoover

By Sarah Murdoch Special to the Star

The top 10 titles on the Original Fiction list are all by and for women— and young women at that: Witness the number of romances and tales of dragon-slaying teenaged girls. Last year there was plenty of romance but not a single fantasy title. We can thank TikTok for drawing together this huge community of adventure-craving readers. On the second half of our Top 20, men wrote just three of the novels: Stephen King (“Holly”), John Grisham (“The Exchange”) and Abraham Verghese (“The Covenant of Water”).

Here’s an interesting anomaly: While only three of 20 authors on the Original Fiction list are men, on the Canadian Fiction list, six of the 20 are men.

The titles on the 2023 Original Non-Fiction list is dominated by biographies and memoirs from both sexes.

Other reflections on the year in books:

*   Last year, romance writer Colleen Hoover held the top two spots with “It Ends with Us” and its sequel, “It Starts with Us.” Same this year. How boring. But her reign on the Fiction list is likely over. Hoover had seven books on the Top 20 list in 2022 but just three (just!) this year (the third, “Ugly Love,” chimes in at No. 15). CoHo was last seen on our regular weekly list on Sept. 6, when “It Ends with Us” ranked No. 10. She also ranks No. 1 on our bestselling Mystery list with “Verity,” beating out novels by veterans Stephen King and John Grisham.
*   Untimely death seems to spur book sales. Note that Matthew Perry’s 2022 memoir “Friends, Lovers and the Big Terrible Thing,” ended the year at No. 4 on the Original non-fiction list, because his death at the end of October sparked renewed interest in his life and travails. The book ended 2022 on the same list at #3.
*   Diversity, equity and inclusion have been hot topics and publishing houses and awards committees have been prompted to search for and encourage books by racialized writers. But has the push for equity paid off financially? The bestselling fiction of the year is almost entirely monochromatic: white women. The two exceptions are Chinese-American writer R.F. Kuang (“Yellowface”) and South-Asian author Abraham Verghese (“The Covenant of Water”). The only diversity on the Original non-fiction list is “Beyond the Story,” a 10 th anniversary coffee-table tome celebrating Korean boy group BTS, and “21 Things You May Not Know about the Indian Act” by Bob Joseph, a member of the Gwawaenuk Nation in British Columbia. The Canadian lists feature a greater representation: Cree writer Michelle Good; Anishinaabe writer Waubgeshig Rice, Suzette Mayr, a writer and academic of German and Afro-Caribbean background, Ted Nolan, a member of the Garden River First Nation Reserve, and writer and former politician Jody Wilson-Raybould, a member of the We Wai Kai Nation of British Columbia.
*   And finally, the top three books of the year, across all categories:

1.“Spare,” by Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex

2.“Twenty Thousand Fleas under the Sea (Dog Man #11)”, by Dav Pilkey

3.“It Starts with Us,” by Colleen Hoover

Source: The Star compiles its bestseller list from sales data supplied by Booknet Canada. It tracks English-language print book sales reported from Canadian booksellers each week.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The American daily newspaper _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ publishes multiple weekly lists ranking the best-selling books in the United States. The lists are split into three genres—fiction, [nonfiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonfiction "Nonfiction") and [children's books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_books "Children's books"). Both the fiction and nonfiction lists are further split into multiple lists.

## Fiction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_New_York_Times_number-one_books_of_2023&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Fiction")]

The following list ranks the number-one best-selling fiction books, in the combined print and e-books category.

The most frequent weekly best seller of the year was _[It Starts with Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_Starts\_with\_Us "It Starts with Us")_ by [Colleen Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colleen_Hoover "Colleen Hoover") with 10 weeks at the top of the list, followed closely by _[Fourth Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth\_Wing "Fourth Wing")_ by [Rebecca Yarros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebecca_Yarros "Rebecca Yarros") with 9 weeks. For a second consecutive year, Colleen Hoover was the most frequent weekly best-selling author with 14 weeks at the top of the list.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The American daily newspaper _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ publishes multiple weekly lists ranking the best-selling books in the United States. The lists are split into three genres—fiction, [nonfiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonfiction "Nonfiction") and [children's books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_books "Children's books"). Both the fiction and nonfiction lists are further split into multiple lists.

## Fiction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_New_York_Times_number-one_books_of_2023&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Fiction")]

The following list ranks the number-one best-selling fiction books, in the combined print and e-books category.

The most frequent weekly best seller of the year was _[It Starts with Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_Starts\_with\_Us "It Starts with Us")_ by [Colleen Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colleen_Hoover "Colleen Hoover") with 10 weeks at the top of the list, followed closely by _[Fourth Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth\_Wing "Fourth Wing")_ by [Rebecca Yarros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebecca_Yarros "Rebecca Yarros") with 9 weeks. For a second consecutive year, Colleen Hoover was the most frequent weekly best-selling author with 14 weeks at the top of the list.

### Best Sellers Methodology

A version of this list appears in the November 19, 2023 issue of[The New York Times Book Review](https://www.nytimes.com/section/books/review). Rankings on weekly lists reflect sales for the week ending November 4, 2023. Lists are published early online.

### Best Sellers Symbol Key

*   Up in Rank since last week

*   Down in Rank since last week

*   If a book is not in a rank since the previous week, it will not have an arrow. The last few titles on the list known as the extended list, never have arrows.

*   An asterisk indicates that a book's sales are barely distinguishable from those of the book above it.

*   A dagger indicates that some retailers report receiving bulk orders.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

The American daily newspaper _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ publishes multiple weekly lists ranking the best-selling books in the United States. The lists are split into three genres—fiction, [nonfiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonfiction "Nonfiction") and [children's books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_books "Children's books"). Both the fiction and nonfiction lists are further split into multiple lists.

## Fiction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_The_New_York_Times_number-one_books_of_2023&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Fiction")]

The following list ranks the number-one best-selling fiction books, in the combined print and e-books category.

The most frequent weekly best seller of the year was _[It Starts with Us](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_Starts\_with\_Us "It Starts with Us")_ by [Colleen Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colleen_Hoover "Colleen Hoover") with 10 weeks at the top of the list, followed closely by _[Fourth Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth\_Wing "Fourth Wing")_ by [Rebecca Yarros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebecca_Yarros "Rebecca Yarros") with 9 weeks. For a second consecutive year, Colleen Hoover was the most frequent weekly best-selling author with 14 weeks at the top of the list.

Fern Brookbanks has wasted far too much of her adult life thinking about Will Baxter. She spent just twenty-four hours in her early twenties with the aggravatingly attractive, idealistic artist, a chance encounter that spiraled into a daylong adventure in the city. The timing was wrong, but their connection was undeniable: they shared every secret, every dream, and made a pact to meet one year later. Fern showed up. Will didn't.  
  
 At thirty-two, Fern's life doesn't look at all how she once imagined it would. Instead of living in the city, Fern's back home, running her mother's lakeside resort — something she vowed never to do. The place is in disarray, her ex-boyfriend's the manager, and Fern doesn't know where to begin.  
  
 She needs a plan — a lifeline. To her surprise, it comes in the form of Will, who arrives nine years too late, with a suitcase in tow and an offer to help on his lips. Will may be the only person who understands what Fern's going through. But how could she possibly trust this expensive-suit wearing mirage who seems nothing like the young man she met all those years ago. Will is hiding something, and Fern's not sure she wants to know what it is.  
  
 But ten years ago, Will Baxter rescued Fern. Can she do the same for him? (_From Viking_)

## [**Why Carley Fortune loves writing romance**](https://www.cbc.ca/radio/thenextchapter/blockbuster-canadian-romance-writer-carley-fortune-dives-into-summer-love-at-the-lake-1.6900306)

"What I love as a romance reader is watching two people who can feel very real going through real problems and trying to figure themselves out, trying to figure another person out and ultimately there is this happy ending _."_

> Ultimately, I want to give people hope.- Carley Fortune

"So you go on this very emotional journey but you feel safe. I needed that when I was reading in 2020, and I needed that as a writer. I think my books do look at tough subjects._Meet Me at the Lake_deals with mental health, with grief and loss. But ultimately, I want to give people hope. I want people to feel like they've snooped on a real relationship and I want to give people an escape."

The timing was wrong, but their connection was undeniable: they shared every secret, every dream, and made a pact to meet one year later. Fern showed up. Will didn't.  
  
 At thirty-two, Fern's life doesn't look at all how she once imagined it would. Instead of living in the city, Fern's back home, running her mother's lakeside resort — something she vowed never to do. The place is in disarray, her ex-boyfriend's the manager, and Fern doesn't know where to begin.  
  
 She needs a plan — a lifeline. To her surprise, it comes in the form of Will, who arrives nine years too late, with a suitcase in tow and an offer to help on his lips. Will may be the only person who understands what Fern's going through. But how could she possibly trust this expensive-suit wearing mirage who seems nothing like the young man she met all those years ago. Will is hiding something, and Fern's not sure she wants to know what it is.  
  
 But ten years ago, Will Baxter rescued Fern. Can she do the same for him? (_From Viking_)

**A random connection sends two strangers on a daylong adventure where they make a promise one keeps and the other breaks, with life-changing effects.**  
  
Fern Brookbanks has wasted far too much of her adult life thinking about Will Baxter. She spent just twenty-four hours in her early twenties with the aggravatingly attractive, idealistic artist, a chance encounter that spiraled into a daylong adventure in the city. The timing was wrong, but their connection was undeniable: they shared every secret, every dream, and made a pact to meet one year later. Fern showed up. Will didn’t.  
  
At thirty-two, Fern’s life doesn’t look at all how she once imagined it would. Instead of living in the city, Fern’s back home, running her mother’s lakeside resort—something she vowed never to do. The place is in disarray, her ex-boyfriend’s the manager, and Fern doesn’t know where to begin.  
  
She needs a plan—a lifeline. To her surprise, it comes in the form of Will, who arrives nine years too late, with a suitcase in tow and an offer to help on his lips. Will may be the only person who understands what Fern’s going through. But how could she possibly trust this expensive-suit wearing mirage who seems nothing like the young man she met all those years ago. Will is hiding something, and Fern’s not sure she wants to know what it is.  
  
But ten years ago, Will Baxter rescued Fern. Can she do the same for him?

Meet Me at the Lake by Carley Fortune  
  
Carley Fortune has entertained me again. Something about her good but flawed characters just work for me. Once again, they hold back, don't say what they need to say, and hurt themselves as much as they hurt others.   
  
Both twenty two and beginning the next stage of their lives, Fern and Will meet for the first time and spend a glorious but bittersweet twenty four hours together. We don't know Will's inner thoughts but we do know Fern's and it's obvious that Will has woken Fern up in a way that needed to happen. In Will, Fern sees what she wants but he's not hers for the taking and she's not free to take. But they have a firm date to meet at her family resort in one year.   
  
Fern spends the year thinking about Will but when the day comes he stands her up. A year before, Will gave Fern what she needed to change the direction of her life. Now his absence at the meeting Fern has longed for all year changes Fern again. Already reeling from past hurts, Fern still can't let go of the memories of that twenty four hours with Will.   
  
Then ten years from the date of first meeting Will, there he is at her family's resort. He's there to help her again, when he's really the one that needs help. But these two can't get the words out to say what needs to be said. Usually I don't like that kind of thing, somehow not disclosing what is important, when to do so could explain so much. Too good to be true Will is here now but still, he seems out of reach even though she can touch him. Will is so likeable but has a wall up in some ways, Fern is so careful to not be hurt again, and then there are the interesting side characters to fill out this world of Will and Fern. I really did like what all the characters could add to this sweet story.

The MMC and FMC hang out with each other for one day and are head over heels for each other. Then they meet each other 10 years later and all those feelings come rushing back- which apparently were never gone in the first place.   
  
I did not mind the plot at all, it was interesting. The **pacing** however dragged, especially in the second half, the first half was okay. The book is evenly divided with the flashbacks and present scenario, as compared to ESA. This time it's more 50-50.   
  
In comparison to ESA, the **characters** are pretty simple to understand, to understand their motives, to understand their immaturity. **The FMC, Fern-** is not that appealing to the reader. She doesn't have the "it factor". Her personality is quite forgettable. Grieving the loss of her mother, she is back in her hometown, trying to run her mother's business and she loves Will- that's all there is to her.   
  
The **MMC, Will-** I liked him. Compared to Fern, he's a complex character and has depth. Also, he has a story to himself. He is the charming, mysterious, broody, sexy and sadly immature type. He confused me at times, he wanted Fern then he didn't, then he did, then he didn't and at last he just accepted he wants her. It frustrated me a lot cause I seriously liked the guy.   
  
Apart from the pacing, what makes me bump down the rating is the drama caused by Will in the **final act-** it's just so damn stupid. I want to keep the review spoiler free so I won't build on it. Another thing that I immensely disliked was the fact that both Will and Fern **cheated** on their significant others and it's apparently being overlooked by a lot of readers just cause it did not happen to the main characters. Fern's emotional cheating 10 years ago over Jamie, and Will's cheating on his gf _oddly named Fred_ is not justified. The main characters do not even discuss it.
