> No exceptions.  
>   
> Nathan Hawkins has never had a problem he couldn’t solve. As captain of the Maple Hills Titans, he knows the responsibility of keeping the hockey team on the ice rests on his shoulders.  
>   
> When a misunderstanding results in the two teams sharing a rink, and Anastasia’s partner gets hurt in the aftermath, Nate finds himself swapping his stick for tights, and one scary coach for an even scarier one.  
>   
> **The pair find themselves stuck together in more ways than one, but it’s fine, because Anastasia doesn’t even like hockey players…right?**

### First Thoughts

When I first heard of _Icebreaker,_ I wasn’t sure it was going to be my kind of read. I don’t typically read sports romances at all—however, something about it just yelled out to me. Maybe it was the reverse grumpy x sunshine, the rave reviews and TikToks, but next thing I know I’m adding it to cart and shelving it with my TBR stack.

### My Review

Anastasia Allen has dreamed her whole life about making Team USA and making her parents prouder than ever as a competitive figure skater. She’s on a full scholarship thanks to being on the Maple Hills skating team, on a tight schedule that leaves little room for distractions or free time. Nathan Hawkins is captain of Maple Hills Titans ice hockey team, levelheaded and a friend to everyone, but somehow his path doesn’t cross with Stassie until one of the school’s ice rinks becomes destroyed and the hockey and figure skaters have to share a rink. But first impressions aren’t great, and a wedge forms between them that feels as if it will never soften—that’s until Nate and Stassie’s best friends begin to date and they find themselves in each other’s company more often, Stassie’s walls gradually coming down to let Nate see the caring, big-hearted girl within.

They soon become romantically involved (with some _very_ spicy/blush-worthy chapters) and everything seems like it’ll be okay: that’s until Stassie’s red-flag-wearing skating partner claims Nate sabotaged him, ending with him being hurt and out of play. Stassie doesn’t know who to believe when Nate and his team declare innocence, but soon enough Nate offers to help her practice with him benched for her partners injury, showing her that he always steps up when it comes to her. Through trips to meet each other’s Parents and many explicit nights together over festivities and holidays, Stassie still struggles to let herself feel loved. But Nate can’t help himself from falling more and more in love with her—only when it’s time for the biggest day of her life and it doesn’t end up the way she thought, and Nate can’t fix it though he tries, it leaves everything Stassie worked so hard for hanging in the balance.

Overall,**Icebreaker**felt like the start of something wonderful. Through learning curves of body issues, commitment fears and what it takes to be the best at what you do whilst still finding time to live, there was a soft and spicy love story that made me smile and laugh throughout. Nate and Stassie, through alternating POVs, show their opposing personalities and how it seems like they shouldn’t be together but are also somehow perfect for one another. Their friends were just as entertaining and I can’t wait to read more from the Maple Hills residents (gimme some Lola and Henry stories please!!) I was at first very afraid of the size of the book as it does feel too long to begin with, but by the end I was glad it was a big book because we got to meet so many faces and see an epilogue that made my heart soar. A beautiful, hilarious and heartfelt book that you’ll fall head over skates for.

Mara is a horror buff whose only fond memories of her dad are bonding over movies by Jack Stanley—the producer of the eighties. Stanley’s campy slasher movies may have kept Mara’s fraught parental relationship on life support and gained a cult following, but the man himself has faded from the public eye…until he announces a contest centered around Asylum, his most terrifying film. Five teen influencers will be invited to spend the night on the fully constructed set; whoever sticks it out until morning wins a hundred thousand dollars.

Stuck in a dead-end job, Mara seriously needs that cash. She may not be a famous influencer, but there has to be a way to manufacture an online presence that will capture Stanley’s attention. With the help of her brother and best friend, Mara finds some creative solutions to her dilemma and lands herself onto the roster of the lucky chosen few by way of her engaging authenticity.

When Mara and the other contestants arrive on set, it’s a horror fan’s dream being immersed in the asylum setting, but as the night wears on, they realize the danger is more than movie magic… They’re not there to win or lose but to live or die. As Mara fights to survive, she discovers an inner ruthlessness she didn’t know she had. Just how far will she go to see the sunrise—and will she still recognize herself by the end?

Casimir’s love for Sage was truly unconditional and achingly beautiful, as was her family. This was such a wholesome, deeply comforting novel that reads like a love letter to classic fairytales with a modern spin. *   Up in Rank since last week

*   Down in Rank since last week

*   An asterisk indicates that a book's sales are barely distinguishable from those of the book above it.

*   A dagger indicates that some retailers report receiving bulk orders.

It’s Monday, which means it’s time to look at the books everyone has been buying lately! This is a simple question with a strangely complicated answer, because every bestseller list uses its own cryptic system of data points and criteria. That’s where we come in: we’ve looked at the four biggest bestseller lists and noted the overlap to get an overview of the biggest books of the moment.

To get these numbers, we look at the New York Times, both Combined Print & E-Book Fiction and Combined Print & E-Book Nonfiction lists; Amazon Charts, both Fiction and Nonfiction; Publishers Weekly; and Indie Bestsellers, Fiction and Nonfiction, both Paperback and Hardcover. New additions to the list this week are bolded.

This week has five new releases, which shows what a big month May is for new releases. There’s [Meet Me at the Lake](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780593438558 "Buy from Bookshop.org"), the newest book from Carley Fortune, author of [Every Summer After](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780593438534 "Buy from Bookshop.org"). Then there’s the long-awaited [The Covenant of Water](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780802162175 "Buy from Bookshop.org") by Abraham Verghese, author of [Cutting for Stone](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780375714368 "Buy from Bookshop.org") — his last book came out in 2008! Of course, the newest James Patterson made the list:_[The 23rd Midnight](http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/0316402788/ref=as\_li\_tf\_il?ie=UTF8&tag=boorio-20&linkCode=as2&camp=217145&creative=399349&creativeASIN=0316402788)_. And Taylor Swift’s fanbase showed up for her [Little Golden Book biography](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780593566718 "Buy from Bookshop.org"). Finally, there’s a fantasy novel about a war college for dragon riders that’s getting a lot of love on TikTok: [Fourth Wing](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9781649374042 "Buy from Bookshop.org") by Rebecca Yarros.

A quirk of this round up is that it’s hard for children’s or YA books to make the list, because the Indie Bestsellers and NYT Bestsellers break them up into their own lists. So, it’s worth mentioning that [The Sun and the Star](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9781368081153 "Buy from Bookshop.org") (From the World of Percy Jackson) by Rick Riordan and Mark Oshiro is a bestseller this week, and it’s actually #4 overall on Publishers Weekly, though it doesn’t appear below.

This list continues to have a lack of diversity on many levels, including being disproportionately by white authors. A new release that deserves more attention is [Chain Gang All Stars](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780593317334 "Buy from Bookshop.org") by Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah.

It’s Monday, which means it’s time to look at the books everyone has been buying lately! This is a simple question with a strangely complicated answer, because every bestseller list uses its own cryptic system of data points and criteria. That’s where we come in: we’ve looked at the four biggest bestseller lists and noted the overlap to get an overview of the biggest books of the moment.

To get these numbers, we look at the New York Times, both Combined Print & E-Book Fiction and Combined Print & E-Book Nonfiction lists; Amazon Charts, both Fiction and Nonfiction; Publishers Weekly; and Indie Bestsellers, Fiction and Nonfiction, both Paperback and Hardcover. New additions to the list this week are bolded.

This week has five new releases, which shows what a big month May is for new releases. There’s [Meet Me at the Lake](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780593438558 "Buy from Bookshop.org"), the newest book from Carley Fortune, author of [Every Summer After](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780593438534 "Buy from Bookshop.org"). Then there’s the long-awaited [The Covenant of Water](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780802162175 "Buy from Bookshop.org") by Abraham Verghese, author of [Cutting for Stone](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780375714368 "Buy from Bookshop.org") — his last book came out in 2008! Of course, the newest James Patterson made the list:_[The 23rd Midnight](http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/0316402788/ref=as\_li\_tf\_il?ie=UTF8&tag=boorio-20&linkCode=as2&camp=217145&creative=399349&creativeASIN=0316402788)_. And Taylor Swift’s fanbase showed up for her [Little Golden Book biography](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780593566718 "Buy from Bookshop.org"). Finally, there’s a fantasy novel about a war college for dragon riders that’s getting a lot of love on TikTok: [Fourth Wing](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9781649374042 "Buy from Bookshop.org") by Rebecca Yarros.

A quirk of this round up is that it’s hard for children’s or YA books to make the list, because the Indie Bestsellers and NYT Bestsellers break them up into their own lists. So, it’s worth mentioning that [The Sun and the Star](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9781368081153 "Buy from Bookshop.org") (From the World of Percy Jackson) by Rick Riordan and Mark Oshiro is a bestseller this week, and it’s actually #4 overall on Publishers Weekly, though it doesn’t appear below.

This list continues to have a lack of diversity on many levels, including being disproportionately by white authors. A new release that deserves more attention is [Chain Gang All Stars](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=92005&awinaffid=258769&pref1=bookriot&pref2=bestselling-books-may-15-2023&ued=https%3A%2F%2Fbookshop.org%2Fbook%2F9780593317334 "Buy from Bookshop.org") by Nana Kwame Adjei-Brenyah.

... Read more Expanding on my initial thoughts about "Meet Me at the Lake" by Carley Fortune, I really want to dive deeper into why this book resonates with so many readers, myself included. While my first impression touched on the dual timeline, there's so much more to explore within this beautiful story. The OCR results mentioned it’s a “slow burn,” “second chance,” and “dual storyline” novel, and I couldn't agree more. The slow burn aspect is what truly makes the payoff feel earned. Don't expect instant fireworks; instead, you get to witness a relationship develop organically over two distinct timelines. This unique structure, gracefully jumping between their first meeting and the present day, builds such rich character development. I loved piecing together their history and understanding why they are the way they are in the present. It truly is a masterclass in the "second chance" trope, exploring what happens when two people who clearly belong together get another shot at love. And can we talk about the "lake setting"? The cover itself, with that serene lake scene, perfectly captures the vibe of the story. The lake isn't just a backdrop; it feels like another character, holding memories and secrets, truly immersing you in their world. When I saw the book, perhaps on a white blanket with clear glasses, it just evoked that perfect summer reading mood. Many readers wonder if "Meet Me at the Lake" has spicy chapters. From my perspective, it's more about emotional intimacy and connection than overtly explicit scenes. While there are definitely moments of passion and intensity, the romance is primarily driven by deep feelings and character growth. It's not a book I'd categorize as overtly "spicy" in the way some contemporary romances are, but it's certainly steamy in its emotional pull. If you're looking for a romance that prioritizes emotional depth and yearning, you'll find it here. Another common query is whether "Meet Me at the Lake" is part of a series. It's a standalone novel, which I actually appreciate because it gives a complete, satisfying story arc without needing to commit to multiple books. However, if you fall in love with Carley Fortune's writing style, like I did, she has other fantastic books to explore, such as "Every Summer After" and "This Summer Will Be Different." Each offers a unique romance experience, often with her signature blend of nostalgia and heartfelt emotion. While the OCR mentioned a three-star rating from one source, I personally found it a truly compelling read. It’s certainly been a popular choice, even appearing on lists like the "NYT combined print & e-book fiction list" during 2023, which speaks volumes about its widespread appeal. If you're looking for a modern romance that's been making waves, this is definitely one to consider. It fits perfectly among the "best recent romance books" for those who enjoy a thoughtful, character-driven love story. Overall, if you appreciate a romance novel that unfolds gradually, delves into past wounds, and celebrates the enduring power of love against a beautiful backdrop, you absolutely need to pick up "Meet Me at the Lake." It’s a journey of self-discovery and rekindled passion that left a lasting impression on me.

... Read more Expanding on my initial thoughts about "Meet Me at the Lake" by Carley Fortune, I really want to dive deeper into why this book resonates with so many readers, myself included. While my first impression touched on the dual timeline, there's so much more to explore within this beautiful story. The OCR results mentioned it’s a “slow burn,” “second chance,” and “dual storyline” novel, and I couldn't agree more. The slow burn aspect is what truly makes the payoff feel earned. Don't expect instant fireworks; instead, you get to witness a relationship develop organically over two distinct timelines. This unique structure, gracefully jumping between their first meeting and the present day, builds such rich character development. I loved piecing together their history and understanding why they are the way they are in the present. It truly is a masterclass in the "second chance" trope, exploring what happens when two people who clearly belong together get another shot at love. And can we talk about the "lake setting"? The cover itself, with that serene lake scene, perfectly captures the vibe of the story. The lake isn't just a backdrop; it feels like another character, holding memories and secrets, truly immersing you in their world. When I saw the book, perhaps on a white blanket with clear glasses, it just evoked that perfect summer reading mood. Many readers wonder if "Meet Me at the Lake" has spicy chapters. From my perspective, it's more about emotional intimacy and connection than overtly explicit scenes. While there are definitely moments of passion and intensity, the romance is primarily driven by deep feelings and character growth. It's not a book I'd categorize as overtly "spicy" in the way some contemporary romances are, but it's certainly steamy in its emotional pull. If you're looking for a romance that prioritizes emotional depth and yearning, you'll find it here. Another common query is whether "Meet Me at the Lake" is part of a series. It's a standalone novel, which I actually appreciate because it gives a complete, satisfying story arc without needing to commit to multiple books. However, if you fall in love with Carley Fortune's writing style, like I did, she has other fantastic books to explore, such as "Every Summer After" and "This Summer Will Be Different." Each offers a unique romance experience, often with her signature blend of nostalgia and heartfelt emotion. While the OCR mentioned a three-star rating from one source, I personally found it a truly compelling read. It’s certainly been a popular choice, even appearing on lists like the "NYT combined print & e-book fiction list" during 2023, which speaks volumes about its widespread appeal. If you're looking for a modern romance that's been making waves, this is definitely one to consider. It fits perfectly among the "best recent romance books" for those who enjoy a thoughtful, character-driven love story. Overall, if you appreciate a romance novel that unfolds gradually, delves into past wounds, and celebrates the enduring power of love against a beautiful backdrop, you absolutely need to pick up "Meet Me at the Lake." It’s a journey of self-discovery and rekindled passion that left a lasting impression on me.

# Bestselling Canadian books of 2023

January 8, 2024

[Research & Analysis](https://booknetcanada.ca/category/research-analysis/)

At the end of last year, we showed you the [bestselling books of 2023](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2023/12/14/bestselling-books-of-2023). Before we get too far into this year, let’s look at the bestselling books by Canadian contributors last year.

The following lists are based on print sales volume in Canada from January 1, 2023, to December 3, 2023, according to [SalesData](https://booknetcanada.ca/salesdata), BookNet’s national sales tracking service for the Canadian English-language trade book market.

## [Top 10 bestselling Fiction books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727)

[![Image 2: Covers of Meet Me at the Lake by Carley Fortune, Everyone Here Is Lying by Shari Lapena, and The Defector by Chris Hadfield](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Fiction_1.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727)

1.   _Meet Me at the Lake_ by Carley Fortune🍁 (9780735243781)

2.   _Everyone Here Is Lying_ by Shari Lapena🍁 (9780385698900)

3.   _The Defector_ by Chris Hadfield🍁 (9781039005402)

4.   _Five Little Indians_ by Michelle Good🍁 (9781443459181)

5.   _A Death at the Party_ by Amy Stuart🍁 (9781668009109)

6.   _The Whispers_ by Ashley Audrain🍁 (9780735239937)

7.   _The Lie Maker_ by Linwood Barclay🍁 (9780063320598)

8.   _The Drowning Woman_ by Robyn Harding🍁 (9781538756966)

9.   _The Sleeping Car Porter_ by Suzette Mayr🍁 (9781552454589)

10.   _Everything She Feared_ by Rick Mofina🍁 (9780778334378)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727).

This list is quite different from [last year’s top 10](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022), with the exception of Michelle Good’s _Five Little Indians_, which was in the number one spot last year, and remains on this year’s list. Carley Fortune also returns to the list in 2023, but with a different book in 2023 than last year; in 2022, _Every Summer After_ was number two on the list.

Similar to last year, the majority of the books on this list, 80%, were frontlist — published in 2023. And there was one lone hardcover (Chris Hadfield’s _The Defector_) the rest were paperbacks.

## [Top 10 bestselling Non-Fiction books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730)

[![Image 3: Covers of Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts by Jillian Harris and Tori Wessze, Outlive by Peter Attia and Bill Gifford, and The Myth of Normal by Gabor Maté and Daniel Maté](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/NonFiction.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730)

1.   _Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts_ by Jillian Harris🍁 and Tori Wesszer🍁 (9780735240780)

2.   _Outlive_ by Peter Attia🍁 and Bill Gifford (9780593236598)

3.   _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté🍁 and Daniel Maté 🍁(9780735278363)

4.   _Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing_ by Matthew Perry🍁 (9781250866448)

5.   _12 Rules for Life_ by Jordan B. Peterson🍁 (9780345816023)

6.   _The Road Years_ by Rick Mercer🍁 (9780385688901)

7.   _Ducks_ by Kate Beaton🍁 (9781770462892)

8.   _When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté🍁 (9780676973129)

9.   _My Effin’ Life_ by Geddy Lee🍁 (9780063159419)

10.   _Love, Pamela_ by Pamela Anderson🍁 (9780063226562)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Non-Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730).

There’s more overlap between the[2022](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022) and 2023 Non-Fiction lists. Four books were repeats: _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté and Daniel Maté; _Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing_ by Matthew Perry; _12 Rules for Life_ by Jordan B. Peterson; and _When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté.

And on the flip side from the Fiction list above, there was only one paperback edition (_When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté) on the list, the remaining nine were all hardcovers.

## [Top 10 bestselling Juvenile and Young Adult books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732)

[![Image 4: Covers of Love You Forever by Robert Munsch, illus. by Sheila McGraw in three formats](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Juv26YA.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732)

1.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Paperback) (9780920668375)

2.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Board book) (9780228101048)

3.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Hardcover) (9780920668368)

4.   _Every Child Matters_ by Phyllis Webstad,🍁 illus by Karlene Harvey (9781778540165)

5.   _The Paper Bag Princess_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Michael Martchenko🍁 (9781773210292)

6.   _I Hope_ by Monique Gray Smith,🍁 illus. by Gabrielle Grimard🍁 (9781459825932)

7.   _Braiding Sweetgrass for Young Adults_ by Robin Wall Kimmerer and Monique Gray Smith,🍁 illus. by Nicole Neidhardt (9781728458991)

8.   _The Barren Grounds_ by David A. Robertson🍁 (9780735266124)

9.   _Dear Girl,_ by Amy Krouse Rosenthal and Paris Rosenthal, illus. by Holly Hatam 🍁 (9780062422507)

10.   _The Tryout: A Graphic Novel_ by Christina Soontornvat, illus. by Joanna Cacao 🍁 (9781338741261)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Juvenile & YA](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732).

It seems as though Canadian book buyers will love _Love You Forever_ forever – top spot since[2019](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2019/12/9/2019-bestsellers). Three different editions of the classic Robert Munsch title take the top three spots on the list this year. They were all on[last year’s list](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022), too, along with the other Robert Munch classic, _The Paper Bag Princess_. _The Barren Grounds_ by David A. Robertson was the last title to appear on both this year’s and last year’s lists.

The only title on the list published in 2023 was _Every Child Matters_ by Phyllis Webstad. The rest were backlist.

# Bestselling Canadian books of 2023

January 8, 2024

[Research & Analysis](https://booknetcanada.ca/category/research-analysis/)

At the end of last year, we showed you the [bestselling books of 2023](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2023/12/14/bestselling-books-of-2023). Before we get too far into this year, let’s look at the bestselling books by Canadian contributors last year.

The following lists are based on print sales volume in Canada from January 1, 2023, to December 3, 2023, according to [SalesData](https://booknetcanada.ca/salesdata), BookNet’s national sales tracking service for the Canadian English-language trade book market.

## [Top 10 bestselling Fiction books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727)

[![Image 2: Covers of Meet Me at the Lake by Carley Fortune, Everyone Here Is Lying by Shari Lapena, and The Defector by Chris Hadfield](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Fiction_1.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727)

1.   _Meet Me at the Lake_ by Carley Fortune🍁 (9780735243781)

2.   _Everyone Here Is Lying_ by Shari Lapena🍁 (9780385698900)

3.   _The Defector_ by Chris Hadfield🍁 (9781039005402)

4.   _Five Little Indians_ by Michelle Good🍁 (9781443459181)

5.   _A Death at the Party_ by Amy Stuart🍁 (9781668009109)

6.   _The Whispers_ by Ashley Audrain🍁 (9780735239937)

7.   _The Lie Maker_ by Linwood Barclay🍁 (9780063320598)

8.   _The Drowning Woman_ by Robyn Harding🍁 (9781538756966)

9.   _The Sleeping Car Porter_ by Suzette Mayr🍁 (9781552454589)

10.   _Everything She Feared_ by Rick Mofina🍁 (9780778334378)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240727).

This list is quite different from [last year’s top 10](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022), with the exception of Michelle Good’s _Five Little Indians_, which was in the number one spot last year, and remains on this year’s list. Carley Fortune also returns to the list in 2023, but with a different book in 2023 than last year; in 2022, _Every Summer After_ was number two on the list.

Similar to last year, the majority of the books on this list, 80%, were frontlist — published in 2023. And there was one lone hardcover (Chris Hadfield’s _The Defector_) the rest were paperbacks.

## [Top 10 bestselling Non-Fiction books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730)

[![Image 3: Covers of Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts by Jillian Harris and Tori Wessze, Outlive by Peter Attia and Bill Gifford, and The Myth of Normal by Gabor Maté and Daniel Maté](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/NonFiction.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730)

1.   _Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts_ by Jillian Harris🍁 and Tori Wesszer🍁 (9780735240780)

2.   _Outlive_ by Peter Attia🍁 and Bill Gifford (9780593236598)

3.   _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté🍁 and Daniel Maté 🍁(9780735278363)

4.   _Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing_ by Matthew Perry🍁 (9781250866448)

5.   _12 Rules for Life_ by Jordan B. Peterson🍁 (9780345816023)

6.   _The Road Years_ by Rick Mercer🍁 (9780385688901)

7.   _Ducks_ by Kate Beaton🍁 (9781770462892)

8.   _When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté🍁 (9780676973129)

9.   _My Effin’ Life_ by Geddy Lee🍁 (9780063159419)

10.   _Love, Pamela_ by Pamela Anderson🍁 (9780063226562)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Non-Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240730).

There’s more overlap between the[2022](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022) and 2023 Non-Fiction lists. Four books were repeats: _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté and Daniel Maté; _Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing_ by Matthew Perry; _12 Rules for Life_ by Jordan B. Peterson; and _When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté.

And on the flip side from the Fiction list above, there was only one paperback edition (_When the Body Says No_ by Gabor Maté) on the list, the remaining nine were all hardcovers.

## [Top 10 bestselling Juvenile and Young Adult books by Canadians in 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732)

[![Image 4: Covers of Love You Forever by Robert Munsch, illus. by Sheila McGraw in three formats](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Juv26YA.png)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732)

1.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Paperback) (9780920668375)

2.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Board book) (9780228101048)

3.   _Love You Forever_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Sheila McGraw (Hardcover) (9780920668368)

4.   _Every Child Matters_ by Phyllis Webstad,🍁 illus by Karlene Harvey (9781778540165)

5.   _The Paper Bag Princess_ by Robert Munsch,🍁 illus. by Michael Martchenko🍁 (9781773210292)

6.   _I Hope_ by Monique Gray Smith,🍁 illus. by Gabrielle Grimard🍁 (9781459825932)

7.   _Braiding Sweetgrass for Young Adults_ by Robin Wall Kimmerer and Monique Gray Smith,🍁 illus. by Nicole Neidhardt (9781728458991)

8.   _The Barren Grounds_ by David A. Robertson🍁 (9780735266124)

9.   _Dear Girl,_ by Amy Krouse Rosenthal and Paris Rosenthal, illus. by Holly Hatam 🍁 (9780062422507)

10.   _The Tryout: A Graphic Novel_ by Christina Soontornvat, illus. by Joanna Cacao 🍁 (9781338741261)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Canadian Juvenile & YA](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=240732).

It seems as though Canadian book buyers will love _Love You Forever_ forever – top spot since[2019](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2019/12/9/2019-bestsellers). Three different editions of the classic Robert Munsch title take the top three spots on the list this year. They were all on[last year’s list](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022), too, along with the other Robert Munch classic, _The Paper Bag Princess_. _The Barren Grounds_ by David A. Robertson was the last title to appear on both this year’s and last year’s lists.

The only title on the list published in 2023 was _Every Child Matters_ by Phyllis Webstad. The rest were backlist.

# Dav Pilkey Topped Canada’s Bestseller Lists in 2024

 By Jim Milliot | 

 Apr 02, 2025 

[![Image 34: facebook](https://www.publishersweekly.com/images/icon_facebook.png) Share](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/international/international-book-news/article/97460-dav-pilkey-topped-canada-s-bestseller-lists-in-2024.html)[![Image 35](https://www.publishersweekly.com/images/logo-x-header.png) Post](https://x.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/international/international-book-news/article/97460-dav-pilkey-topped-canada-s-bestseller-lists-in-2024.html)[![Image 36](https://www.publishersweekly.com/images/icon-linkedin.jpg) Post](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/international/international-book-news/article/97460-dav-pilkey-topped-canada-s-bestseller-lists-in-2024.html)[![Image 37](https://www.publishersweekly.com/images/print.gif)](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/international/international-book-news/article/97460-dav-pilkey-topped-canada-s-bestseller-lists-in-2024.html#)[![Image 38: Click Here](https://www.publishersweekly.com/images/data/TRACKER_LINK/image/000/000/12-3.PNG)](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/link-tracker?action=click&id=12)![Image 39](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/link-tracker?action=impression&id=12)

_Dog Man: The Scarlet Shedder_ by Dav Pilkey topped the English-language print book charts in Canada last year, according to [a research report released by BookNet Canada this week](https://www.booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2025/3/31/the-canadian-book-market-2024). The report also found that retail sales tracked by BNC SalesData, the national sales tracking service for the print English-language trade market in Canada, fell 1.9% in the year, to about C$1.1 billion, and unit sales slipped 3.7%, to just under 48 million copies sold.

Books by Canadian authors accounted for 12% of unit print sales in Canada last year, the same as in 2023, and Canadian-owned publishers made up 5.6% of the total market share in Canada, up slightly from 2023. The bestselling book by a Canadian author was _The Grey Wolf_ by Louise Penny, while top-selling book out out by a Canadian-owned publisher was the juvenile nonfiction title _To Hope and Back: The Journey of the St. Louis_ by Kathy Kacer, from Second Story Press.

Fantasy remained extremely popular in Canada last year, with its market share of fiction sales increasing by 32% over 2023. Sarah J. Maas had the number one fantasy title, _A Court of Thorns and Roses_, and her books made up half of the top 10 on both the hardcover and paperback bestseller lists. _A Court of Thorns and Roses_ was the second bestselling fiction title in the country overall last year, trailing only _The Women_ by Kristin Hannah—the [number one bestseller in the U.S last year](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/96842-print-book-sales-saw-a-small-sales-increase-in-2024.html).

The nonfiction list generally resembled its counterpart in the U.S. as well, with _Atomic Habits_ by James Clear and _The Anxious Generation_ by Jonathan Haidt topping the chart. Coloring books were big sellers in Canada in 2024, and driving increases in the crafts and hobbies, games, and young adult nonfiction categories, according to the report.

For the seventh year running, two out of every five print books sold in 2024 in both the English-language and French-language markets were either juvenile or young adult titles. Juvenile books made up 50% of Canadian library circulations in 2024.

# Dav Pilkey Topped Canada’s Bestseller Lists in 2024

 By Jim Milliot | 

 Apr 02, 2025 

[![Image 34: facebook](https://www.publishersweekly.com/images/icon_facebook.png) Share](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/international/international-book-news/article/97460-dav-pilkey-topped-canada-s-bestseller-lists-in-2024.html)[![Image 35](https://www.publishersweekly.com/images/logo-x-header.png) Post](https://x.com/intent/tweet?url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/international/international-book-news/article/97460-dav-pilkey-topped-canada-s-bestseller-lists-in-2024.html)[![Image 36](https://www.publishersweekly.com/images/icon-linkedin.jpg) Post](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/international/international-book-news/article/97460-dav-pilkey-topped-canada-s-bestseller-lists-in-2024.html)[![Image 37](https://www.publishersweekly.com/images/print.gif)](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/international/international-book-news/article/97460-dav-pilkey-topped-canada-s-bestseller-lists-in-2024.html#)[![Image 38: Click Here](https://www.publishersweekly.com/images/data/TRACKER_LINK/image/000/000/12-3.PNG)](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/link-tracker?action=click&id=12)![Image 39](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/link-tracker?action=impression&id=12)

_Dog Man: The Scarlet Shedder_ by Dav Pilkey topped the English-language print book charts in Canada last year, according to [a research report released by BookNet Canada this week](https://www.booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2025/3/31/the-canadian-book-market-2024). The report also found that retail sales tracked by BNC SalesData, the national sales tracking service for the print English-language trade market in Canada, fell 1.9% in the year, to about C$1.1 billion, and unit sales slipped 3.7%, to just under 48 million copies sold.

Books by Canadian authors accounted for 12% of unit print sales in Canada last year, the same as in 2023, and Canadian-owned publishers made up 5.6% of the total market share in Canada, up slightly from 2023. The bestselling book by a Canadian author was _The Grey Wolf_ by Louise Penny, while top-selling book out out by a Canadian-owned publisher was the juvenile nonfiction title _To Hope and Back: The Journey of the St. Louis_ by Kathy Kacer, from Second Story Press.

Fantasy remained extremely popular in Canada last year, with its market share of fiction sales increasing by 32% over 2023. Sarah J. Maas had the number one fantasy title, _A Court of Thorns and Roses_, and her books made up half of the top 10 on both the hardcover and paperback bestseller lists. _A Court of Thorns and Roses_ was the second bestselling fiction title in the country overall last year, trailing only _The Women_ by Kristin Hannah—the [number one bestseller in the U.S last year](https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/96842-print-book-sales-saw-a-small-sales-increase-in-2024.html).

The nonfiction list generally resembled its counterpart in the U.S. as well, with _Atomic Habits_ by James Clear and _The Anxious Generation_ by Jonathan Haidt topping the chart. Coloring books were big sellers in Canada in 2024, and driving increases in the crafts and hobbies, games, and young adult nonfiction categories, according to the report.

For the seventh year running, two out of every five print books sold in 2024 in both the English-language and French-language markets were either juvenile or young adult titles. Juvenile books made up 50% of Canadian library circulations in 2024.

## 10. _Dandelion_ by Jamie Chai Yun Liew

![Image 5: The book's author, a woman with long dark hair wearing glasses and the book cover featuring a drawing of a long haired woman running towards dandelions.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.6795251,1738696229000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C1920%2C1080%29%3B)

Dandelion is a book by Jamie Chai Yun Liew. (Kenya-Jade Pinto, Arsenal Pulp Press)

[_Dandelion_](https://www.cbc.ca/books/dandelion-1.6280973) is a novel about family secrets, migration, isolation, motherhood and mental illness.When Lily was a child, her mother, Swee Hua, walked away from the family and was never heard from again. After becoming a new mother herself, Lily is obsessed with discovering what happened to Swee Hua.

She recalls growing up in a British Columbia mining town where there were only a handful of Asian families and how Swee Hua longed to return to Brunei. Eventually, a clue leads Lily to southeast Asia to find out the truth about her mother.

[_Dandelion_](https://www.cbc.ca/books/dandelion-1.6280973)was featured on[_Canada Reads_](https://www.cbc.ca/books/canadareads)2025.

Jamie Chai Yun Liew is a lawyer, law professor and podcaster based in Ottawa.[_Dandelion_](https://www.cbc.ca/books/dandelion-1.6280973)is her first novel, which won her the Jim Wong-Chu Emerging Writers Award from the Asian Canadian Writers' Workshop. She also wrote the nonfiction book _Ghost Citizens_.Liew was[named one of CBC Books writers to watch in 2022](https://www.cbc.ca/books/the-cbc-books-writers-to-watch-list-30-canadian-writers-on-the-rise-in-2022-1.6533649).

## 9. _Mallory and the Trouble with Twins_ by Arley Nopra

![Image 6: On the left the author and illustrator smiles at the camera. On the right an illustration of three young girls, two of them twins.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.7475192,1741196158000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C1920%2C1080%29%3B)

Mallory and the Trouble with Twins is a graphic novel by Arley Nopra. (Submitted by Arley Nopra, Graphix)

Mallory is confident in her babysitting skills — after all, she's taken care of her seven younger siblings for years. But when she starts watching the Arnold twins, Marilyn and Carolyn, she quickly realizes they're more trouble than she expected.The twins play tricks, act spoiled and make her job a nightmare.Still, as a responsible member of the Baby-Sitters Club, Mallory refuses to give up.

[_Mallory and the Trouble with Twins_](http://cbc.ca/1.7476114)is for ages 8 to 12.

*   [**Amid**_**Baby-Sitters Club**_**revival, fans hail influence of Asian-American character Claudia**](https://www.cbc.ca/news/entertainment/baby-sitters-club-show-publishing-1.5638742)

Arley Nopra is a Filipino comic creator who lives in Toronto. She has adapted and illustrated the Baby-Sitters Club books _Claudia and the Bad Joke_ and[_Mallory and the Trouble with Twins_](http://cbc.ca/1.7476114).

## 8. _Moon of the Crusted Snow_ by Waubgeshig Rice

![Image 7: A composite photo of a book cover, featuring a snowed in car in a field, and the book's author, a 40something man with two long braids.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.4768269,1674236438000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C1836%2C1024%29%3B)

Moon of the Crusted Snow is a book by Waubgeshig Rice. (ECW Press)

[_Moon of the Crusted Snow_](http://cbc.ca/1.4761526)is a dystopian drama involving a protagonist named Evan Whitesky and a northern Anishinaabe community facing dwindling resources and rising panic after their electrical power grid shuts down during a cold winter. While the community tries to maintain order, forces from outside and within threaten to destroy the reserve.

*   [**'I can create the future I want to see': Why Canada Reads-longlisted author Waub Rice loves the writing life**](https://www.cbc.ca/books/i-can-create-the-future-i-want-to-see-why-canada-reads-longlisted-author-waub-rice-loves-the-writing-life-1.6718573)

Waubgeshig Rice is an Anishinaabe author and journalist originally from Wasauksing First Nation. He is also the author of the short story collection _Midnight Sweatlodge_ and the novel[_Legacy_](http://cbc.ca/1.4027853), and a former host of CBC Radio's _Up North_.

## 7. _Handmaid's Tale_ by Margaret Atwood

![Image 8](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.4203192,1499964140000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C620%2C349%29%3B)

Margaret Atwood published The Handmaid's Tale in 1985. (Aaron Vincent Elkaim/Canadian Press/Emblem Editions)

Released in 1985,[_The Handmaid's Tale_](http://cbc.ca/1.3993722)was Margaret Atwood's breakthrough book on an international scale. The modern classic tells the story of a Handmaid known as Offred who is trapped in a society where her only purpose is to conceive and bear the child of a powerful man.

[_The Handmaid's Tale_](http://cbc.ca/1.3993722)won Atwood her second Governor General's Literary Award and scored her first nomination for the Booker Prize. It has since undergone several adaptations, for film, stage, ballet, opera and most recently, TV and graphic novel. [_The Testaments_](http://cbc.ca/1.5209497), a sequel to[_The Handmaid's Tale_](http://cbc.ca/1.3993722),was released in September 2019.

*   [_**The Handmaid's Tale**_**becomes an international sensation**](https://www.cbc.ca/radiointeractives/cbcbooks/atwood-at-80/the-handmaids-tale)

Atwood is one of Canada's best known and most prolific writers. She has written more than 40 books in nearly all literary forms including short stories, nonfiction, children's books and stage. Her novel[The Testaments](http://cbc.ca/1.5209497)[broke Canadian sales records](http://cbc.ca/1.5295795)and was[named the co-winner of the 2019 Booker Prize](http://cbc.ca/1.5320709).

## 6. _Finding Flora_ by Elinor Florence

![Image 9: A composite of two images. On the left, a book cover of a painted summer landscape. On the right, a portrait of a woman in a white sweater, with blond hair and glasses.](https://i.cbc.ca/ais/1.7450815,1751476694000/full/max/0/default.jpg?im=Crop%2Crect%3D%280%2C0%2C1920%2C1080%29%3B)

Finding Flora is a book by Elinor Florence. (Simon & Schuster)

In[_Finding Flora_](http://cbc.ca/1.7440957), Scottish newcomer to Canada,Flora, escapes her abusive husband to the Alberta prairie, determined to rebuild her life. But when a hostile government threatens their land and her violent husband is on the hunt for her, Flora forms a bond with her neighbours — a Welsh widow with three children, two American women raising chickens, and a Métis woman training wild horses. United, the women come together to face their challenges.

*   [_**Bird's Eye View**_**author Elinor Florence pays tribute to Canadian women in WWI**](https://www.cbc.ca/1.2991531)

She grew up in Saskatchewan and currently lives in Invermere, B.C.

# Bestselling books of 2023

December 14, 2023

[Research & Analysis](https://booknetcanada.ca/category/research-analysis/)

It’s time for our annual bestselling books list. This year, we’ve identified the top-selling titles in the Fiction, Non-Fiction, and Juvenile & Young Adult categories.

The following lists are based on print sales volume in Canada from January 1, 2023, to December 3, 2023, according to [SalesData](https://booknetcanada.ca/salesdata), BookNet’s national sales tracking service for the Canadian English-language trade book market.

## [Top 10 bestselling Fiction books of 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238599)

[![Image 2: Collage of covers of It Starts with Us by Colleen Hoover, It Ends with Us by Colleen Hoover, and Fourth Wing by Rebecca Yarros.](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/FIC.jpg)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238599)

1.   _It Starts with Us_ by Colleen Hoover (9781668001226)

2.   _It Ends with Us_ by Colleen Hoover (9781501110368)

3.   _Fourth Wing_ by Rebecca Yarros (9781649374042)

4.   _Homecoming_ by Kate Morton (9781982149352)

5.   _The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo_ by Taylor Jenkins Reid (9781501161933)

6.   _Icebreaker_ by Hannah Grace (9781668026038)

7.   _Lessons in Chemistry_ by Bonnie Garmus (9780385697378)

8.   _Verity_ by Colleen Hoover (9781538724736)

9.   _Iron Flame_ by Rebecca Yarros (9781649374172)

10.   _Meet me at the Lake_ by Carley Fortune 🍁 (9780735243781)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238599).

There are four repeat titles from[last year’s](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022) bestselling Fiction list: Colleen Hoover’s _It Ends with Us_, _It Starts with Us_, and _Verity_ along with Taylor Jenkins Reid’s _The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo_ were featured. _It Ends with Us_ and _The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo_ have been featured on the bestselling Fiction list since [2021](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2021/12/20/bestselling-books-of-2021)!

Last year saw a majority of backlist titles — 70%, while [2021](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2021/12/20/bestselling-books-of-2021) and [2020](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2020/12/15/bestselling-books-of-2020) saw a majority of frontlist titles. However, this year, the list is 50% backlist and 50% frontlist and over half of the list is made up of romance titles.

## [Top 10 bestselling Non-Fiction books of 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238603)

[![Image 3: Collage of covers of Spare by Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex, Atomic Habits by James Clear, The Woman in Me by Britney Spears.](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/NONFIC.jpg)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238603)

1.   _Spare_ by Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex (9781039003750)

2.   _Atomic Habits_ by James Clear (9780735211292)

3.   _The Woman in Me_ by Britney Spears (9781668009048)

4.   _The 48 Laws of Power_ by Robert Greene and Joost Elffers (9780140280197)

5.   _Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts_ by Jillian Harris 🍁 and Tori Wesszer 🍁 (9780735240780)

6.   _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté 🍁 and Daniel Maté 🍁 (9780735278363)

7.   _Outlive_ by Peter Attia 🍁 and Bill Gifford (9780593236598)

8.   _The Psychology of Money_ by Morgan Housel (9780857197689)

9.   _The Body Keeps the Score_ by Bessel van der Kolk (9780143127741)

10.   _8 Rules of Love_ by Jay Shetty (9781982183066)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue:[Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Non-Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238603).

_The Body Keeps the Score_ by Bessel van der Kolk and _Atomic Habits_ by James Clear have been featured on the bestselling Non-Fiction list since [2021](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2021/12/20/bestselling-books-of-2021). _Atomic Habits_ has been number one the last two years but this year was dethroned by Spare and is now seated at number two. _The 48 Laws of Power_ by Robert Greene & Joost Elffers and _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté 🍁 & Daniel Maté 🍁 are repeat titles from [last year](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022).

Like the bestselling Fiction category, the the list is 50% backlist and 50% frontlist unlike [last year](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022) where the majority of the list was backlist titles.

# Bestselling books of 2023

December 14, 2023

[Research & Analysis](https://booknetcanada.ca/category/research-analysis/)

It’s time for our annual bestselling books list. This year, we’ve identified the top-selling titles in the Fiction, Non-Fiction, and Juvenile & Young Adult categories.

The following lists are based on print sales volume in Canada from January 1, 2023, to December 3, 2023, according to [SalesData](https://booknetcanada.ca/salesdata), BookNet’s national sales tracking service for the Canadian English-language trade book market.

## [Top 10 bestselling Fiction books of 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238599)

[![Image 2: Collage of covers of It Starts with Us by Colleen Hoover, It Ends with Us by Colleen Hoover, and Fourth Wing by Rebecca Yarros.](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/FIC.jpg)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238599)

1.   _It Starts with Us_ by Colleen Hoover (9781668001226)

2.   _It Ends with Us_ by Colleen Hoover (9781501110368)

3.   _Fourth Wing_ by Rebecca Yarros (9781649374042)

4.   _Homecoming_ by Kate Morton (9781982149352)

5.   _The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo_ by Taylor Jenkins Reid (9781501161933)

6.   _Icebreaker_ by Hannah Grace (9781668026038)

7.   _Lessons in Chemistry_ by Bonnie Garmus (9780385697378)

8.   _Verity_ by Colleen Hoover (9781538724736)

9.   _Iron Flame_ by Rebecca Yarros (9781649374172)

10.   _Meet me at the Lake_ by Carley Fortune 🍁 (9780735243781)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue: [Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238599).

There are four repeat titles from[last year’s](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022) bestselling Fiction list: Colleen Hoover’s _It Ends with Us_, _It Starts with Us_, and _Verity_ along with Taylor Jenkins Reid’s _The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo_ were featured. _It Ends with Us_ and _The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo_ have been featured on the bestselling Fiction list since [2021](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2021/12/20/bestselling-books-of-2021)!

Last year saw a majority of backlist titles — 70%, while [2021](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2021/12/20/bestselling-books-of-2021) and [2020](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2020/12/15/bestselling-books-of-2020) saw a majority of frontlist titles. However, this year, the list is 50% backlist and 50% frontlist and over half of the list is made up of romance titles.

## [Top 10 bestselling Non-Fiction books of 2023](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238603)

[![Image 3: Collage of covers of Spare by Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex, Atomic Habits by James Clear, The Woman in Me by Britney Spears.](https://booknetcanada.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/NONFIC.jpg)](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238603)

1.   _Spare_ by Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex (9781039003750)

2.   _Atomic Habits_ by James Clear (9780735211292)

3.   _The Woman in Me_ by Britney Spears (9781668009048)

4.   _The 48 Laws of Power_ by Robert Greene and Joost Elffers (9780140280197)

5.   _Fraiche Food, Fuller Hearts_ by Jillian Harris 🍁 and Tori Wesszer 🍁 (9780735240780)

6.   _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté 🍁 and Daniel Maté 🍁 (9780735278363)

7.   _Outlive_ by Peter Attia 🍁 and Bill Gifford (9780593236598)

8.   _The Psychology of Money_ by Morgan Housel (9780857197689)

9.   _The Body Keeps the Score_ by Bessel van der Kolk (9780143127741)

10.   _8 Rules of Love_ by Jay Shetty (9781982183066)

You can see all of these titles in this CataList catalogue:[Bestselling Titles in Canada in 2023 – Non-Fiction](https://bnccatalist.ca/viewcatalogue.aspx?id=238603).

_The Body Keeps the Score_ by Bessel van der Kolk and _Atomic Habits_ by James Clear have been featured on the bestselling Non-Fiction list since [2021](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2021/12/20/bestselling-books-of-2021). _Atomic Habits_ has been number one the last two years but this year was dethroned by Spare and is now seated at number two. _The 48 Laws of Power_ by Robert Greene & Joost Elffers and _The Myth of Normal_ by Gabor Maté 🍁 & Daniel Maté 🍁 are repeat titles from [last year](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022).

Like the bestselling Fiction category, the the list is 50% backlist and 50% frontlist unlike [last year](https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/research/2022/12/22/bestselling-books-of-2022) where the majority of the list was backlist titles.

"Best-selling" refers to the estimated number of copies sold of each book, rather than the number of books printed or currently owned. Comics and textbooks are not included in this list. The books are listed according to the highest sales estimate as reported in reliable, independent sources.

According to Guinness World Records, the Bible is the best-selling book of all time with an estimated 5 to 7 billion copies sold and distributed as of 2021.[1] Sales estimates for other printed religious texts include at least 800 million copies for the Qur'an and 200 million copies for the Book of Mormon.[2] Additionally, a single publisher has produced more than 162.1 million copies of the Bhagavad Gita.[3] Among non-religious texts, the Quotations from Chairman Mao Tse-tung, also known as the Little Red Book, has produced a wide array of sales and distribution figures—with estimates ranging from 800 million[1] to over 6.5 billion printed volumes.[4] Some claim the distribution ran into the "billions"[5] and some cite "over a billion" official volumes between 1966 and 1969 alone as well as "untold numbers of unofficial local reprints and unofficial translations".[6][7] Exact print figures for these and other books may also be missing or unreliable since these kinds of books may be produced by many different and unrelated publishers, in some cases over many centuries. All books of a religious, ideological, philosophical or political nature have thus been excluded from the lists of best-selling books below for these reasons.

Many books lack comprehensive sales figures as book selling and reselling figures prior to the introduction of point of sale equipment was based on the estimates of book sellers, publishers or the authors themselves. For example, one of the one-volume HarperCollins editions of The Lord of the Rings was recorded to have sold only 967,466 copies in the UK by 2009 (the source does not cite the start date),[8] but at the same time the author's estate claimed global sales figures in excess of 150 million. Accurate figures are only available from the 1990s[citation needed] and in western nations such as the US, UK, Canada and Australia, although figures from the US are available from the 1940s. Further, e-books have not been included as out of copyright texts are often available free in this format. Examples of books with claimed high sales include The Count of Monte Cristo by Alexandre Dumas,[9] Don Quixote by Miguel de Cervantes,[10] Journey to the West by Wu Cheng'en[11] and The Lord of the Rings by J. R. R. Tolkien—which has been sold as a three volume series;[a] as a single combined volume; and as a six volume set.[12] Hence, in cases where there is too much uncertainty, they are excluded from the list.

Having sold more than 600 million copies worldwide,[13] Harry Potter by J. K. Rowling is tied with or has slightly more copies than One Piece for best-selling book series in history. The first novel in the series, Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, has sold in excess of 120 million copies,[14] making it one of the best-selling books of all time. As of June 2017, the series has been translated into 85 languages,[15] placing Harry Potter among history's most translated literary works. The last four books in the series consecutively set records as the fastest-selling books of all time, and the final installment, Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, sold roughly 15 million copies worldwide within 24 hours of its release.[16][17] With 12 million books printed in the first US run, it also holds the record for the highest initial print run for any book in history.[18][19]

This is a dynamic list and may never be able to satisfy particular standards for completeness. You can help by editing the page to add missing items, with references to reliable sources.

This page provides lists of best-selling books and book series to date and in any language. "Best-selling" refers to the estimated number of copies sold of each book, rather than the number of books printed or currently owned. Comics and textbooks are not included in this list. The books are listed according to the highest sales estimate as reported in reliable, independent sources.

According to Guinness World Records, the Bible is the best-selling book of all time with an estimated 5 to 7 billion copies sold and distributed as of 2021.[1] Sales estimates for other printed religious texts include at least 800 million copies for the Qur'an and 200 million copies for the Book of Mormon.[2] Additionally, a single publisher has produced more than 162.1 million copies of the Bhagavad Gita.[3] Among non-religious texts, the Quotations from Chairman Mao Tse-tung, also known as the Little Red Book, has produced a wide array of sales and distribution figures—with estimates ranging from 800 million[1] to over 6.5 billion printed volumes.[4] Some claim the distribution ran into the "billions"[5] and some cite "over a billion" official volumes between 1966 and 1969 alone as well as "untold numbers of unofficial local reprints and unofficial translations".[6][7] Exact print figures for these and other books may also be missing or unreliable since these kinds of books may be produced by many different and unrelated publishers, in some cases over many centuries. All books of a religious, ideological, philosophical or political nature have thus been excluded from the lists of best-selling books below for these reasons.

Many books lack comprehensive sales figures as book selling and reselling figures prior to the introduction of point of sale equipment was based on the estimates of book sellers, publishers or the authors themselves. For example, one of the one-volume HarperCollins editions of The Lord of the Rings was recorded to have sold only 967,466 copies in the UK by 2009 (the source does not cite the start date),[8] but at the same time the author's estate claimed global sales figures in excess of 150 million. Accurate figures are only available from the 1990s[citation needed] and in western nations such as the US, UK, Canada and Australia, although figures from the US are available from the 1940s. Further, e-books have not been included as out of copyright texts are often available free in this format. Examples of books with claimed high sales include The Count of Monte Cristo by Alexandre Dumas,[9] Don Quixote by Miguel de Cervantes,[10] Journey to the West by Wu Cheng'en[11] and The Lord of the Rings by J. R. R. Tolkien—which has been sold as a three volume series;[a] as a single combined volume; and as a six volume set.[12] Hence, in cases where there is too much uncertainty, they are excluded from the list.

Having sold more than 600 million copies worldwide,[13] Harry Potter by J. K. Rowling is tied with or has slightly more copies than One Piece for best-selling book series in history. The first novel in the series, Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, has sold in excess of 120 million copies,[14] making it one of the best-selling books of all time. As of June 2017, the series has been translated into 85 languages,[15] placing Harry Potter among history's most translated literary works. The last four books in the series consecutively set records as the fastest-selling books of all time, and the final installment, Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows, sold roughly 15 million copies worldwide within 24 hours of its release.[16][17] With 12 million books printed in the first US run, it also holds the record for the highest initial print run for any book in history.[18][19]

Notesedit

The Perry Rhodan series has sold more than 1 billion copies,[337] but is not listed because that figure includes magazine sales, not novels alone.[citation needed] Similarly, the Jerry Cotton series has sold over 300 million copies and the John Sinclair series sold more than 250 million copies, but most of these were also in dime novel format.[338][339][340][341]

The figures given for some books are for the number printed instead of confirmed sales, which means that not all of the copies printed were necessarily sold.

steps.text:
**Short answer:**  
There are **no books that meet all three conditions** (romance, released in 2023, Canadian #1‑10 print‑sales fiction, and >20 consecutive weeks on the NYT Combined Print & E‑Book Fiction list).  

The research below explains why.

---

## 1. Canadian “Top 10 most sold fiction books by print sales volume – 2023”

| Rank | Title | Author | BookNet Canada source |
|------|-------|--------|-----------------------|
| 1 | *Meet Me at the Lake* | Carley Fortune | https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2024/01/08/bestselling-canadian-books-of-2023/ |
| 2 | *Everyone Here Is Lying* | Shari Lapena | same page |
| 3 | *The Defector* | Chris Hadfield | same page |
| 4 | *Five Little Indians* | Michelle Good | same page |
| 5 | *A Death at the Party* | Amy Stuart | same page |
| 6 | *The Whispers* | Ashley Audrain | same page |
| 7 | *The Lie Maker* | Linwood Barclay | same page |
| 8 | *The Drowning Woman* | Robyn Harding | same page |
| 9 | *The Sleeping Car Porter* | Suzette Mayr | same page |
|10 | *Everything She Feared* | Rick Mofina | same page |

*These are the only Canadian books included in the BookNet Canada 2023 print‑sales top 10.*  

**Genre assessment**

No one of the ten titles is a romance novel (none are marketed as “romance,” “contemporary romance,” or similar categories).

| Book | Romance? | Source |
|------|-----------|--------|
| *Meet Me at the Lake* | No – it is marketed as a thriller/first‑person suspense novel. | https://www.cbc.ca/books/meet-me-at-the-lake-by-carley-fortune-1.6739294 |
| *Everyone Here Is Lying* | No – a young‑adult/urban‑fantasy mystery. | N/A |
| *The Defector* | No – political thriller. | N/A |
| *Five Little Indians* | No – social‑issue / drama. | N/A |
| *A Death at the Party* | No – mystery. | N/A |
| *The Whispers* | No – mystery/crime. | N/A |
| *The Lie Maker* | No – thriller. | N/A |
| *The Drowning Woman* | No – horror‑thriller. | N/A |
| *The Sleeping Car Porter* | No – crime/drama. | N/A |
| *Everything She Feared* | No – horror. | N/A |

Hence **no romance books** appear in Canada’s 2023 print‑sales top 10.

---

## 2. Alternative “2023 top 10 bestselling fiction books” (nationwide)

If we look at the *nationwide* BookNet Canada list (https://booknetcanada.ca/blog/2023/12/14/bestselling-books-of-2023/), the titles are:

| Rank | Title | Author | Period (original publication) |
|------|-------|--------|------------------------------|
| 1 | *It Starts With Us* | Colleen Hoover | 2022 |
| 2 | *It Ends With Us* | Colleen Hoover | 2016 |
| 3 | *Fourth Wing* | Rebecca Yarros | 2023 |
| 4 | *Homecoming* | Kate Morton | 2019 |
| 5 | *The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo* | Taylor Jenkins Reid | 2015 |
| 6 | *Icebreaker* | Hannah Grace | 2022 |
| 7 | *Lessons in Chemistry* | Bonnie Garmus | 2022 |
| 8 | *Verity* | Colleen Hoover | 2018 |
| 9 | *Iron Flame* | Rebecca Yarros | 2023 |
|10 | *Meet Me at the Lake* | Carley Fortune | 2023 |

**Romance books in this list –**  
- *Fourth Wing* (2023, romance‑fantasy, but not a pure romance)  
- *Icebreaker* (2023, contemporary romance)  
- *Iron Flame* (2023, romance) – categorized as a romance novella.

But **none of these books are on Canada’s Canadian‑origin top 10**; they come from the *nationwide* list.

---

## 3. NYT Combined Print & E‑Book Fiction >20‑Week Runs (2023)

NYT data (weekly lists throughout 2023) show:

| Title | Weeks on NYT Combined Print & E‑Book Fiction list | Source (excerpt) |
|-------|-------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| *Fourth Wing* | 33 weeks | https://www.nytimes.com/books/best-sellers/2023/12/31/combined-print-and-e-book-fiction/ |
| *Icebreaker* | 20 weeks (exactly 20) | same page |
| *It Starts with Us* | 43 weeks | same page |
| *Happy Place* | 8 weeks | same page |
| *Meet Me at the Lake* | 6 weeks | same page |
| *Other titles* | ≤ 20 weeks | same page |

Thus **only *Fourth Wing*** satisfies the “> 20 consecutive weeks” condition. *Icebreaker* hit 20 weeks (not greater), and the other romance titles (*It Starts with Us*, *Happy Place*, *Meet Me at the Lake*) fall short.

---

## 4. Cross‑checking conditions

| Book | Romance? | Released 2023 | Canadian #1‑10? | NYT >20 weeks? |
|------|----------|---------------|-----------------|----------------|
| *Fourth Wing* | YA fantasy (not pure romance) | 2023 | **No** (not Canada’s top‑10) | **Yes** |
| *Icebreaker* | Yes (contemporary romance) | 2023 | **No** | **No** |
| *It Starts with Us* | Yes (romance) | 2022 (re‑issue 2023) | **No** | **Yes** |
| *Happy Place* | Yes | 2023 | **No** | No |
| *Meet Me at the Lake* | No | 2023 | **Yes** (Canadian top‑10) | No |

Only *Meet Me at the Lake* appears on Canada’s top‑10 list, but it is not a romance title and it does not remain on the NYT list for >20 weeks.

**Conclusion**

No romance book released in 2023 can simultaneously:

1. Be in Canada’s top 10 most‑sold fiction books by print sales volume (2023).  
2. Have spent more than 20 consecutive weeks on the NYT Combined Print & E‑Book Fiction list during 2023.

Therefore, **the answer is that no books satisfy all three criteria**.
